```text
1	---
2	name: dvc-ml-workflow
3	description: Set up and operate a DVC (Data Version Control) workflow for ML projects — `dvc init`, `dvc.yaml` pipelines, `params.yaml`, `dvc exp run --queue` for parallel sweeps with metrics auto-bound to ephemeral git commits, and remote storage (S3/SSH/GDrive). Use whenever the user wants reproducible ML pipelines, data/model versioning that lives alongside git, parameter sweeps without standing up a tracking server, queued/parallel experiment execution, or asks about `dvc.yaml` / `dvc exp run` / `dvc queue` / `params.yaml` / `dvc add` / `dvc push` / `.dvc/cache`. Always references the official docs at https://dvc.org/doc and the upstream repo https://github.com/treeverse/dvc (Iterative was acquired by Treeverse in 2024 — `pip install dvc` resolves to this repo).
4	---
5	
6	# DVC ML Workflow
7	
8	DVC turns a git repo into a full ML lab: data and model files are versioned out-of-band (in a cache + remote), pipelines are declared in `dvc.yaml`, and experiments are run as ephemeral git commits with metrics and plots attached. No tracking server, no separate database — everything lives in your existing git history.
9	
10	This skill is opinionated about **the parts of DVC that matter for production ML work**: pipelines, queued experiments, metrics/commit binding, and remotes. It defers to the official docs at https://dvc.org/doc for everything else and links them inline so the agent always pulls the latest guidance.
11	
12	## When to use
13	
14	- User wants reproducible ML pipelines without a tracking server (`mlflow`, `wandb`, etc.)
15	- User mentions `dvc.yaml`, `params.yaml`, `dvc exp run`, `dvc queue`, `dvc push`, `.dvc/cache`
16	- User wants to do a hyperparameter sweep / grid search and have each run land as a separate commit with metrics
17	- User wants to version a dataset or model file too large for git
18	- User asks "how do I make my training reproducible" and is already on git
19	- User wants `mlflow ui`-style experiment comparison but **doesn't want to run a server** (DVC's `dvc exp show` + VS Code extension fills that role)
20	
21	## When NOT to use
22	
23	- User wants a hosted experiment dashboard with multi-user collaboration → use `mlflow-tracking` skill
24	- User wants LLM trace observability (spans, prompts, token costs) → DVC has no story here; use `mlflow-tracking`
25	- User just needs `git lfs` for a few large files → DVC is overkill; recommend `git lfs`
26	- User has an existing `mlflow` workflow and is happy with it → don't push DVC unless they ask
27	
28	## Authoritative sources (always link these, don't paraphrase from memory)
29	
30	- Docs root: https://dvc.org/doc
31	- Command reference: https://dvc.org/doc/command-reference
32	- User guide: https://dvc.org/doc/user-guide
33	- Upstream repo: https://github.com/treeverse/dvc (formerly `iterative/dvc`; redirects)
34	- PyPI: https://pypi.org/project/dvc/
35	
36	When you're unsure of a flag, syntax, or behavior, **fetch the relevant doc page** rather than guessing — DVC's CLI surface changes between minor versions.
37	
38	## Core mental model
39	
40	Three orthogonal things, often confused:
41	
42	| DVC concept | Analogy | What it does |
43	|---|---|---|
44	| `dvc add <file>` | `git lfs track` | Snapshots a single file/dir into the cache, writes a `.dvc` pointer file (which **is** committed to git) |
45	| `dvc.yaml` (stages) | `Makefile` | Declares pipeline stages with dependencies and outputs; `dvc repro` re-runs only stages whose inputs changed |
46	| `dvc exp run` | `git commit` for experiments | Runs the pipeline once with optional param overrides, captures metrics + outputs as an **ephemeral commit** |
47	
48	The non-obvious bit: `dvc exp run` builds on top of `dvc.yaml`. You don't choose between "use pipelines" and "run experiments" — you write the pipeline once, then launch many experiments against it.
49	
50	## Workflow
51	
52	### 1. Initialize the project
53	
54	Use the bundled helper (handles `.gitignore`, sample files, optional remote):
55	
56	```bash
57	bash skills/local/dvc-ml-workflow/scripts/init-dvc-project.sh
58	# or with a remote:
59	bash skills/local/dvc-ml-workflow/scripts/init-dvc-project.sh --remote s3://my-bucket/dvc-store
60	```
61	
62	Manual equivalent (only do this if the helper doesn't fit):
63	
64	```bash
65	dvc init                              # creates .dvc/, .dvcignore
66	git add .dvc .dvcignore
67	git commit -m "Initialize DVC"
68	```
69	
70	For a sub-project inside a monorepo that already has its own `.git`, use `dvc init --subdir`. See [Gotchas](#gotchas).
71	
72	### 2. Track data and models
73	
74	```bash
75	dvc add data/raw/             # snapshot a directory
76	dvc add models/best.pt        # snapshot a single model file
77	git add data/raw.dvc models/best.pt.dvc .gitignore
78	git commit -m "Track raw data and best model"
79	```
80	
81	The `.dvc` files are tiny pointers (md5 + path). The actual bytes go to `.dvc/cache/`. **Never** `git add` anything inside `.dvc/cache/` — it's gitignored automatically and would defeat the purpose.
82	
83	### 3. Define a pipeline (`dvc.yaml`)
84	
85	Use `params.yaml` for hyperparameters. Use `dvc stage add` to declare stages — never hand-edit `dvc.yaml` from scratch unless you've already used `dvc stage add` enough times to know the schema.
86	
87	```bash
88	dvc stage add -n featurize \
89	  -d src/featurize.py -d data/raw \
90	  -o data/features \
91	  python src/featurize.py
92	
93	dvc stage add -n train \
94	  -d src/train.py -d data/features -p model.lr,model.epochs \
95	  -o models/best.pt \
96	  -M metrics.json --plots-no-cache plots.csv \
97	  python src/train.py
98	```
99	
100	The `-M` flag marks a file as a **metrics file** (auto-bound to the experiment commit). `--plots-no-cache` marks a file as a plot source (rendered by `dvc plots show`).
101	
102	For schema details and `foreach` matrix stages, **read** `references/pipelines-and-stages.md`.
103	
104	### 4. Run experiments (the queue is the killer feature)
105	
106	For a single run:
107	
108	```bash
109	dvc exp run                           # uses current params.yaml
110	dvc exp run -S model.lr=1e-3          # override one param
111	dvc exp run -S 'model.lr=range(1e-4,1e-2,3)'  # NOT valid — see queue below
112	```
113	
114	For a **sweep**, queue + start workers:
115	
116	```bash
117	# Enqueue a grid (each -S adds one experiment to the queue):
118	dvc exp run --queue -S model.lr=1e-4
119	dvc exp run --queue -S model.lr=5e-4
120	dvc exp run --queue -S model.lr=1e-3
121	
122	# Start 3 parallel workers — they each pick one queued experiment:
123	dvc queue start --jobs 3
124	
125	# Watch progress:
126	dvc queue status
127	dvc queue logs <task-id>             # if one fails
128	
129	# When done:
130	dvc exp show                          # tabular view of all experiments
131	```
132	
133	Each completed experiment is an **ephemeral commit** in `refs/exps/...`. Metrics, params, and outputs are bundled with it. Promote one to a real commit with `dvc exp apply <exp-name>` then `git commit`.
134	
135	For grids, queue helpers, and ephemeral-vs-real commit semantics, **read** `references/experiments-and-queue.md`.
136	
137	### 5. Push artifacts to a remote
138	
139	```bash
140	dvc remote add -d origin s3://my-bucket/dvc-store    # -d = default
141	dvc push                                             # upload cache to remote
142	git push                                             # share the .dvc pointers
143	```
144	
145	Anyone who clones can `dvc pull` to get the actual bytes. For S3 / GCS / Azure / SSH / GDrive specifics and credential handling, **read** `references/data-and-remotes.md`.
146	
147	### 6. Compare and visualize
148	
149	```bash
150	dvc exp show                          # table of all experiments
151	dvc exp show --csv | column -t -s,    # human-readable
152	dvc metrics show                      # current workspace metrics
153	dvc metrics diff HEAD~1               # compare against last commit
154	dvc plots show                        # render plots from --plots files
155	dvc plots diff HEAD~1                 # overlay current vs prior plots
156	```
157	
158	For plot templates (Vega-Lite), confusion matrices, and the VS Code extension, **read** `references/plots-and-metrics.md`.
159	
160	## Available scripts
161	
162	- **`scripts/init-dvc-project.sh`** — Idempotent project init. `dvc init` + `.gitignore` for `.dvc/cache/` + optional `dvc remote add` + drops the `dvc.yaml` / `params.yaml` / `.dvcignore` templates from `assets/` if missing.
163	  - Flags: `--remote URL`, `--subdir`, `--force`, `--dry-run`, `--help`
164	- **`scripts/queue-helper.sh`** — Wraps `dvc queue` subcommands with structured JSON stdout (one object per task) so an agent can grep/filter task status without parsing tabular output.
165	  - Subcommands: `enqueue PARAM=VAL,...`, `start --jobs N`, `status`, `logs TASK_ID`
166	  - Flags: `--help`, `--json` (default for `status`)
167	- **`scripts/lint-dvcyaml.sh`** — Validates `dvc.yaml` by running `dvc dag --dot` (parse-only, no execution). Exits non-zero with the parse error if the schema is broken.
168	  - Flags: `--help`
169	
170	## Bundled assets
171	
172	- `assets/dvc.yaml.template` — Minimal 2-stage pipeline (`featurize` → `train`) with metrics and plots wired up correctly.
173	- `assets/params.yaml.template` — Nested params for `data` / `model` / `train` sections (the `-S model.lr=...` override syntax keys off this nesting).
174	- `assets/.dvcignore.template` — Sensible defaults: ignore notebooks, scratch dirs, `__pycache__`, etc.
175	
176	## Reference files
177	
178	- `references/pipelines-and-stages.md` — Read **when** writing or debugging `dvc.yaml`: stage schema, `foreach`, `vars`, `wdir`, `frozen`, `always_changed`, and the difference between `-d` / `-o` / `-M` / `--plots`.
179	- `references/experiments-and-queue.md` — Read **when** the user wants sweeps, parallel runs, or asks how metrics get bound to commits. Covers `dvc exp run --queue`, `dvc queue start --jobs`, `dvc exp apply` / `branch` / `remove` / `gc`, and ephemeral-commit semantics.
180	- `references/data-and-remotes.md` — Read **when** setting up `dvc remote` or troubleshooting `dvc push` / `dvc pull`. Covers S3, SSH, GDrive, Azure, GCS, MinIO (S3-compatible), credentials via env / `dvc remote modify --local`.
181	- `references/plots-and-metrics.md` — Read **when** the user asks about visualization, dashboards, or VS Code integration. Covers `dvc plots show / diff`, custom Vega-Lite templates, confusion matrices, and `dvc.api.metrics_show()` for programmatic access.
182	
183	## Gotchas
184	
185	- **`dvc init` fails inside an existing repo's subdirectory** unless you pass `--subdir`. Symptom: `ERROR: '.git' or '.hg' directory not found`. The helper script handles this — manually, do `dvc init --subdir`.
186	- **`dvc exp run --queue` only enqueues; it does not run.** Until you call `dvc queue start`, queued experiments sit idle. The agent will sometimes report "experiment finished" because the enqueue succeeded — verify with `dvc queue status`.
187	- **`dvc.lock` MUST be committed.** It records the exact md5s of inputs/outputs for each stage. If you `.gitignore` it, `dvc repro` becomes non-deterministic between machines. Conversely, **`.dvc/cache/` MUST NOT be committed** (it's the actual data — that goes to the remote).
188	- **Metrics file format matters.** `-M metrics.json` expects a flat JSON object (`{"acc": 0.91, "loss": 0.3}`) or a one-level-nested one. YAML works too. Free-form text won't render in `dvc exp show`.
189	- **`dvc push` silently succeeds if the remote is misconfigured but credentials are missing** for some backends — it just reports "0 files pushed" without an error code in older versions. Always verify with `dvc status -c` (cloud status) after the first push from a new machine.
190	- **Param overrides use dot-notation against `params.yaml` keys.** `-S lr=1e-3` only works if `lr` is at the top level. If you nested it under `model:`, you must use `-S model.lr=1e-3`.
191	- **macOS port 8080 / Iterative Studio**: if the user mentions Iterative Studio, note that it's now a separate Treeverse-managed product, not bundled with `dvc` itself. Don't conflate the two.
192	- **`dvc queue start` runs jobs in the background.** Closing your terminal does NOT kill them (they're detached). Use `dvc queue kill <task-id>` to stop one.
193
```

1	---
2	name: marimo-batch-mlflow
3	description: Prepare a marimo notebook to run as both an interactive UI and a scheduled batch script, using Tyro for CLI parsing (with dataclass or Pydantic params) and MLflow for experiment tracking. Use when the user wants the same marimo notebook to serve as both a UI for iteration and a CLI script for batch jobs / hyperparameter sweeps, and prefers Tyro over `mo.cli_args()` and MLflow over Weights and Biases. For the upstream W&B + `mo.cli_args()` variant, see marimo-team/skills/skills/marimo-batch.
4	---
5	
6	# marimo-batch-mlflow
7	
8	Opinionated fork of [marimo-team/skills/marimo-batch](https://github.com/marimo-team/skills/tree/main/skills/marimo-batch) that:
9	
10	1. Uses **[Tyro](https://brentyi.github.io/tyro/)** for CLI parsing (works with `dataclass`, `pydantic.BaseModel`, or `attrs`) instead of `mo.cli_args()` + manual help-table rendering.
11	2. Uses **[MLflow](https://mlflow.org/)** + **[mlflow-widgets](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/mlflow-widgets)** for experiment tracking instead of Weights and Biases.
12	3. Keeps the dual-mode pattern (`mo.app_meta().mode == "script"`) so a single `notebook.py` is both the UI for iteration and the entry point for `uv run notebook.py --epochs 50` batch jobs.
13	
14	## When to use this vs upstream `marimo-batch`
15	
16	| Concern | upstream `marimo-batch` | this skill |
17	|---|---|---|
18	| CLI parsing | `mo.cli_args()` + hand-rolled `rich.Table` for `--help` | `tyro.cli(ModelParams)` — auto `--help`, type coercion, validation |
19	| Params model | Pydantic `BaseModel` | `dataclass` (primary) or `pydantic.BaseModel` (alternative) |
20	| Tracking backend | Weights and Biases (`wandb`) | MLflow (`mlflow` + optional `mlflow-widgets` for live charts) |
21	| Live training UI | none — W&B web dashboard only | `mlflow_widgets.MlflowChart` cell, gated off in script mode |
22	| Grid launcher | HF Jobs + `WANDB_API_KEY` secret | HF Jobs + `MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI` (+ optional `MLFLOW_TRACKING_TOKEN`) |
23	
24	Pick this skill when the user has a self-hosted MLflow server (or local `./mlruns` is fine) and prefers strongly-typed CLIs. Pick upstream when the user is already on W&B.
25	
26	## Dual-mode pattern
27	
28	The single source-of-truth idiom: branch on `mo.app_meta().mode == "script"` once, build `params` either from a form or from CLI flags, then **let every downstream cell consume `params` regardless of source**.
29	
30	```python
31	import marimo as mo
32	
33	is_script_mode = mo.app_meta().mode == "script"
34	
35	if is_script_mode:
36	    params = tyro.cli(ModelParams)
37	else:
38	    mo.stop(form.value is None, mo.md("*Submit the form to start training.*"))
39	    params = ModelParams(**form.value)
40	
41	# Every cell below uses `params.epochs`, `params.batch_size`, ...
42	# unaware of which branch produced it.
43	```
44	
45	This is what makes the notebook usable as both a UI for fast iteration and a CLI script for sweeps without code duplication.
46	
47	## Params with dataclass + Tyro (primary)
48	
49	```python
50	from dataclasses import dataclass
51	import tyro
52	
53	@dataclass
54	class ModelParams:
55	    """Model training parameters."""
56	    epochs: int = 25
57	    """Number of training epochs."""
58	    batch_size: int = 32
59	    """Training batch size."""
60	    learning_rate: float = 1e-4
61	    """Learning rate for AdamW."""
62	    mlflow_experiment: str = "batch-sizes"
63	    """MLflow experiment name (empty string disables logging)."""
64	    mlflow_run_name: str | None = None
65	    """Optional explicit run name; auto-derived from params if None."""
66	
67	if is_script_mode:
68	    params = tyro.cli(ModelParams)
69	```
70	
71	Tyro derives `--epochs INT`, `--batch-size INT`, etc., from the field names; PEP 257 docstrings under each field become CLI help text. `--help` is generated automatically — no `rich.Table` boilerplate needed.
72	
73	CLI usage:
74	
75	```bash
76	uv run notebook.py --epochs 50 --batch-size 64 --learning-rate 5e-4
77	uv run notebook.py --help     # auto-generated
78	```
79	
80	## Params with Pydantic (alternative)
81	
82	Tyro v0.8+ supports `pydantic.BaseModel` directly. Trade `dataclass` for Pydantic when you need field-level validators or `@computed_field`:
83	
84	```python
85	from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
86	import tyro
87	
88	class ModelParams(BaseModel):
89	    epochs: int = Field(default=25, description="Number of training epochs.")
90	    batch_size: int = Field(default=32, description="Training batch size.")
91	    learning_rate: float = Field(default=1e-4, description="Learning rate.")
92	    mlflow_experiment: str = Field(default="batch-sizes")
93	
94	params = tyro.cli(ModelParams)  # same call site
95	```
96	
97	`Field(description=...)` becomes CLI help. See [`references/params-pydantic.py`](references/params-pydantic.py) for the cell-level diff against the dataclass version.
98	
99	## MLflow tracking
100	
101	Wrap the training loop in `mlflow.start_run()`. Default to graceful degradation when `MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI` is unset (MLflow falls back to `./mlruns/`). Disable logging entirely by setting `params.mlflow_experiment = ""`.
102	
103	```python
104	import mlflow
105	import os
106	
107	tracking_uri = os.environ.get("MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI")
108	if tracking_uri:
109	    mlflow.set_tracking_uri(tracking_uri)
110	if params.mlflow_experiment:
111	    mlflow.set_experiment(params.mlflow_experiment)
112	
113	run_ctx = mlflow.start_run(run_name=params.mlflow_run_name) if params.mlflow_experiment else None
114	
115	if run_ctx:
116	    mlflow.log_params({k: v for k, v in vars(params).items() if not k.startswith("mlflow_")})
117	
118	for epoch in range(params.epochs):
119	    avg_loss = train_one_epoch(...)
120	    if run_ctx:
121	        mlflow.log_metric("loss", avg_loss, step=epoch)
122	
123	if run_ctx:
124	    mlflow.end_run()
125	```
126	
127	Use `with mlflow.start_run(...) as run:` if you don't need conditional disable.
128	
129	## Live training widget (UI mode only)
130	
131	In edit mode, embed `mlflow_widgets.MlflowChart` so the user sees the loss curve update live as the training cell runs. Gate it off in script mode (no display surface):
132	
133	```python
134	from mlflow_widgets import MlflowChart
135	
136	if not is_script_mode and params.mlflow_experiment:
137	    chart = MlflowChart(
138	        tracking_uri=os.environ.get("MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI", "file:./mlruns"),
139	        experiment_name=params.mlflow_experiment,
140	        metric_key="loss",
141	    )
142	    widget = mo.ui.anywidget(chart)
143	    widget
144	```
145	
146	For comparing finished runs, swap `MlflowChart` → `MlflowRunTable` or `MlflowParallelCoordinates`. See [mlflow-widgets README](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/mlflow-widgets) for the full surface.
147	
148	## Environment Variables (EnvConfig)
149	
150	Keep upstream's `wigglystuff.EnvConfig` pattern but swap secrets:
151	
152	```python
153	from wigglystuff import EnvConfig
154	import mlflow
155	
156	env_config = mo.ui.anywidget(
157	    EnvConfig({
158	        "MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI": lambda u: mlflow.MlflowClient(tracking_uri=u).search_experiments(),
159	        "MLFLOW_TRACKING_TOKEN": lambda _: True,  # presence-only check
160	    })
161	)
162	env_config if not is_script_mode else None
163	```
164	
165	Place the `EnvConfig` cell near the top of the notebook, after imports, before the params form.
166	
167	## Columns
168	
169	Preserve upstream's column convention for navigability:
170	
171	```python
172	@app.cell(column=0, hide_code=True)
173	def _(mo):
174	    mo.md(r"""## Notebook Description""")
175	    return
176	```
177	
178	Recommended layout: `column=0` description + envs, `column=1` params form, `column=2` data setup, `column=3` model, `column=4` training loop + live chart.
179	
180	## Grid search
181	
182	For hyperparameter sweeps point users at [`references/grid.py`](references/grid.py). Same contract as upstream:
183	
184	- Dry run by default: `uv run grid.py` prints sampled combinations.
185	- `--launch` actually submits jobs.
186	- `--count N` and `--seed S` control sampling.
187	- Backend: Hugging Face Jobs via `huggingface_hub.run_uv_job`. Required secrets: `HF_TOKEN` and `MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI` (instead of upstream's `WANDB_API_KEY`).
188	
189	Swap HF Jobs for Modal / RunPod / local `subprocess.run([...])` by replacing the `run_uv_job` call — the rest of the script (search space, dedup, dry-run formatting) is provider-agnostic.
190	
191	## Workflow when the user invokes this skill
192	
193	1. Confirm the user wants the MLflow + Tyro variant (not upstream W&B + `mo.cli_args()`).
194	2. Ask which params they want exposed as CLI flags.
195	3. Ask: dataclass or Pydantic? Default to dataclass unless they need validators.

197	5. Verify proposed cell-level edits with the user before applying. Keep `@app.cell(column=N, hide_code=True)` markers intact.
198	6. If they want a sweep, copy `references/grid.py` next to their notebook and update the `SEARCH_SPACE` dict.

5	
6	# mkdocs-site-bootstrap
7	
8	Bootstrap and (optionally) deploy a MkDocs Material documentation site for a
9	repository, then keep helping the user add pages over time.
10	
11	This skill is **consent-gated**. It records the user's preferences in
12	`.skills/preferences.yaml` and never repeats destructive actions without
13	asking. If the user changes their mind, `scripts/check-preferences.sh --reset
14	mkdocs_site_bootstrap` clears the recorded decision so the next invocation
15	starts fresh.
16	
17	## When to trigger
18	
19	- User asks to "set up docs", "create a docs site", "add a documentation
20	  site", "publish docs to GitHub Pages"
21	- User has loose markdown notes / a `docs/` directory and wants it browsable
22	- User wants the same docs stack as the `daviddwlee84/agent-skills` repo
23	  applied to a new project
24	- User says they want an LLM-friendly docs site (llms.txt, copy-to-LLM)
25	
26	## When NOT to trigger
27	
28	- User just wants to write a single doc file → don't scaffold a whole site
29	- User explicitly opted out (preferences.yaml says `enabled: false`) → defer
30	  unless the user is now reversing that decision
31	- User wants to evaluate or benchmark a skill → use `skill-creator`
32	- User wants to author a new agent skill → use `skill-author`
33	
34	## Workflow
35	
36	### 1. Read preferences first
37	
38	Before doing anything, check whether this repo already has a recorded
39	decision:
40	
41	```bash
42	bash skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/check-preferences.sh \
43	  --get mkdocs_site_bootstrap
44	```
45	
46	Possible states:
47	
48	| State | Meaning | What to do |
49	|---|---|---|
50	| File doesn't exist or key missing | Never asked | Proceed to step 2 (interview) |
51	| `enabled: true, pages_deployed: true` | Site is live | Skip to step 6 (ongoing helpers) |
52	| `enabled: true, pages_deployed: false` | Bootstrapped but not deployed | Skip to step 5 (deploy) |
53	| `enabled: false` | User opted out | Confirm they want to reverse that, then `--reset` and re-run |
54	
55	### 2. Interview (only if no recorded decision)
56	
57	Ask the user explicitly:
58	
59	1. "Do you want a MkDocs Material documentation site for this project?
60	   (yes / no / I'll think about it)"
61	2. If yes: "Should it auto-deploy to GitHub Pages on push to main?
62	   (yes / no — I'll deploy manually)"
63	
64	Record both answers immediately so an interrupted session doesn't lose them:
65	
66	```bash
67	bash skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/check-preferences.sh \
68	  --set mkdocs_site_bootstrap.enabled=true \
69	  --set mkdocs_site_bootstrap.stack=mkdocs-material \
70	  --set mkdocs_site_bootstrap.auto_deploy=true
71	```
72	
73	If the user said no, record `enabled: false` and stop. Don't pester on
74	future invocations.
75	
76	### 3. Detect existing docs (consent gate)
77	
78	Before scaffolding, scan the target repo. Read
79	`references/existing-docs-handling.md` for the full decision tree, but
80	the short version:
81	
82	- If `mkdocs.yml` already exists → report "looks like an mkdocs site already
83	  exists at <path>; not overwriting" and stop.
84	- If `docs/` exists and is non-empty → list the files, ask the user one of:
85	  (a) skip — leave my docs alone, just create `mkdocs.yml` pointing at them;
86	  (b) wrap — create `mkdocs.yml` with my files included as-is in the nav;
87	  (c) manual — let me reorganize first, then re-run.
88	- If neither exists → safe to scaffold from scratch.
89	
90	Record the decision under `mkdocs_site_bootstrap.existing_docs_decision`.
91	
92	### 4. Scaffold
93	
94	Run `init-docs-site.sh`. It writes (or refuses to overwrite) `mkdocs.yml`,
95	`pyproject.toml` (with `[project.optional-dependencies] docs = […]`), the
96	`docs/` skeleton, `.github/workflows/docs.yml`, and stub assets for
97	copy-to-llm.
98	
99	```bash
100	bash skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/init-docs-site.sh \
101	  --site-name "My Project" \
102	  --repo-slug owner/repo \
103	  --site-url https://owner.github.io/repo/
104	```
105	
106	Use `--dry-run` first to preview. The script always preserves any existing
107	files unless `--force` is passed.
108	
109	After scaffolding, run a local strict build to catch obvious issues:
110	
111	```bash
112	uv sync --extra docs
113	uv run mkdocs build --strict
114	```
115	
116	### 5. Enable Pages and trigger first deploy (consent gate)
117	
118	This calls the GitHub API (`gh api -X POST .../pages -f build_type=workflow`)
119	and then triggers the workflow. **Always confirm with the user first** —
120	say exactly which API call you're about to make and which repo it'll affect.
121	Only proceed on explicit yes.
122	
123	```bash
124	bash skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/enable-pages.sh \
125	  --repo owner/repo
126	```
127	
128	Flags:
129	- `--dry-run` — print the `gh` calls without running them
130	- `--no-trigger` — enable Pages but don't run the workflow yet
131	
132	After success, set `pages_deployed=true` and `pages_enabled_at=$(date +%F)`
133	in preferences.
134	
135	### 6. Ongoing: add docs pages
136	
137	For each new doc the user wants, use the helper instead of hand-editing
138	`mkdocs.yml`:
139	
140	```bash
141	bash skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/add-docs-page.sh \
142	  --section workflows \
143	  --title "My new workflow" \
144	  --slug my-new-workflow
145	```
146	
147	It creates `docs/<section>/<slug>.md` from the page template and inserts a
148	nav entry into `mkdocs.yml` under the matching section heading. Idempotent
149	— re-running with the same slug is a no-op.
150	
151	## Available scripts
152	
153	- **`scripts/check-preferences.sh`** — Read, set, or reset
154	  `.skills/preferences.yaml`. Always-safe to run.
155	  - Flags: `--get KEY`, `--set KEY=VALUE` (repeatable), `--reset NAMESPACE`,
156	    `--list`, `--dry-run`, `--json`.
157	- **`scripts/init-docs-site.sh`** — Scaffold the site files.
158	  - Flags: `--site-name`, `--repo-slug`, `--site-url`, `--existing skip|wrap`,
159	    `--no-workflow`, `--dry-run`, `--force`.
160	- **`scripts/enable-pages.sh`** — Enable Pages and trigger first deploy via
161	  `gh api`. Requires `gh auth status` to pass first.
162	  - Flags: `--repo OWNER/REPO`, `--no-trigger`, `--dry-run`.
163	- **`scripts/add-docs-page.sh`** — Create a new page and insert it into
164	  `mkdocs.yml`'s nav.
165	  - Flags: `--section`, `--title`, `--slug`, `--template PATH`, `--dry-run`,
166	    `--force`.
167	
168	## Reference files
169	
170	- `references/preferences-schema.md` — Schema for
171	  `.skills/preferences.yaml` and conventions for cross-skill use. Read this
172	  whenever you're touching a preferences key for the first time.
173	- `references/existing-docs-handling.md` — Full decision tree for handling
174	  user's pre-existing `docs/` content without surprises. Read this **before
175	  step 3** of every fresh bootstrap.
176	- `references/docs-stack-recipe.md` — Verbatim stack recipe (mkdocs.yml,
177	  pyproject.toml, workflow, linking rules). Useful when the user asks "what
178	  exactly is this stack?" or wants to apply pieces manually.
179	
180	## Bundled assets
181	
182	Templates the scripts copy from. Edit them here, not in the user's repo.
183	
184	- `assets/mkdocs.yml.template` — Material theme + llmstxt + copy-to-llm
185	  plugins + pymdownx.snippets, parameterized with `{{SITE_NAME}}`,
186	  `{{REPO_SLUG}}`, `{{SITE_URL}}`.
187	- `assets/pyproject.toml.template` — Minimal `[project]` block + the docs
188	  optional-deps group.
189	- `assets/docs-workflow.yml.template` — `.github/workflows/docs.yml` with
190	  paths filter, uv setup, strict build, Pages deploy.
191	- `assets/docs-skeleton/` — `index.md`, `getting-started.md`, `_snippets/`
192	  examples, `assets/copy-to-llm/` JS+CSS files copied from this repo.
193	- `assets/page.md.template` — Used by `add-docs-page.sh`.
194	
195	## Gotchas
196	
197	- **MkDocs strict mode rejects relative `.md` links pointing outside
198	  `docs/`.** Inside `docs/` → relative is fine. Outside `docs/` for
199	  `.md` files (e.g., linking to repo `TODO.md`) → use absolute GitHub URL.
200	  Outside `docs/` for directories or non-`.md` (`backlog/`, `pyproject.toml`)
201	  → relative is downgraded to INFO and tolerated. Templates already do this
202	  right; don't "fix" the absolute URLs.
203	- **`pymdownx.snippets` requires `_snippets/` in `not_in_nav:`** or strict
204	  mode complains about pages-not-in-nav. Template handles it.
205	- **`gh api -X POST .../pages` is idempotent for `build_type=workflow`** but
206	  errors on `404 Not Found` if the repo isn't pushed to GitHub yet. Check
207	  `gh repo view` succeeds before running `enable-pages.sh`.
208	- **The Pages deploy workflow needs `permissions: pages: write,
209	  id-token: write`** at the workflow level. Template has it; if you copy
210	  pieces into an existing workflow, don't lose this.
211	- **`copy-to-llm` plugin's `repo_url` is the SITE URL, not the GitHub URL.**
212	  Counter-intuitive name.
213	- **Don't auto-migrate existing user docs.** Always ask. Migrating someone's
214	  hand-curated `docs/` into a new structure is a high-trust action that
215	  should be the user's explicit decision, not the agent's default.
216	- **`.skills/preferences.yaml` is per-repo, not global.** Don't write it to
217	  `~/.skills/` or `~/.config/`. Each repo has its own decisions.
218	
219	## Updating an existing site (not bootstrapping)
220	
221	If `mkdocs.yml` already exists, this skill mostly defers — only
222	`add-docs-page.sh` and `check-preferences.sh` are useful. Don't try to
223	"upgrade" the user's mkdocs.yml without an explicit ask; their config may
224	have customizations the templates don't know about.

2	name: project-knowledge-harness
3	description: Set up a structured project memory for any software project — TODO.md as priority/effort-tagged index of future work, backlog/ for resume-friendly research/design notes on P? items, and pitfalls/ as a symptom-grep-able knowledge base of past traps. Use when a user wants somewhere to record "maybe later" ideas, freeze troubleshooting state, capture trade-off analysis, or stop re-debugging the same problem.
4	---
5	
6	# project-knowledge-harness
7	
8	A lightweight, file-based memory harness for any software project.
9	
10	Three surfaces, sharply separated by **time direction** and **access pattern**:
11	
12	| Surface | Time | Question it answers | Access pattern |
13	|---|---|---|---|
14	| `TODO.md` | Future | "What might we do later?" | Read top to bottom (priority lanes) |
15	| `backlog/<slug>.md` | Future | "What was the analysis behind this idea?" | Indexed from `TODO.md` |
16	| `pitfalls/<slug>.md` | **Past** | **"I see error X — has this happened before?"** | **Grep symptom keywords** |
17	
18	Plus, in projects that already have agent contracts, `AGENTS.md` Hard
19	invariants answer "What rules MUST agents follow?". Pitfalls *graduate* to
20	Hard invariants when serious enough — see
21	[`references/when-to-add-docs.md`](references/when-to-add-docs.md).
22	
23	## When to use this skill
24	
25	Use this skill when the user surfaces any of:
26	
27	- A long-term TODO list with no home, or a messy `TODO.md` that needs
28	  structure (signals: "where should ideas go?", "maybe later", "工程量太大需要再評估")
29	- A debugging session worth saving (signals: "keep solving the same problem
30	  twice", "save this troubleshooting", "踩過的坑", "TROUBLESHOOTING.md
31	  scattered across docs/")
32	- A request to consolidate `IDEAS.md` / `ROADMAP.md` / `WISHLIST.md` /
33	  `LESSONS.md` files
34	
35	Do NOT use this skill for active sprint planning (use issue trackers),
36	ephemeral agent scratchpads (use `.claude/plans/`), or current feature
37	documentation (use `docs/`).
38	
39	## How to apply this skill (default workflow)
40	
41	The skill bundles five scripts and several templates. **Default to the
42	init script** for setup, and **default to `add-todo.sh` / `sweep-inbox.sh`
43	for capture** rather than asking the agent to edit `TODO.md` by hand.
44	
45	```
46	scripts/
47	  init.sh         # one-shot setup of TODO.md + backlog/ + pitfalls/
48	                  # + agent guidance + README snippet
49	  todo-kanban.sh  # validate TODO.md format and render kanban-style board
50	  add-todo.sh     # insert a structured entry into the right ## P* lane
51	  promote-todo.sh # move an active TODO item to ## Done with the right syntax
52	  sweep-inbox.sh  # triage backlog/inbox.md into TODO.md via add-todo.sh
53	```
54	
55	### 1. Run `scripts/init.sh` against the target repo
56	
57	```sh
58	scripts/init.sh \
59	  --target /path/to/project \
60	  --project-name "My Project" \
61	  --deployment chezmoi   # or npm | pip | docker | none
62	```
63	
64	The script:
65	
66	1. Creates `TODO.md`, `backlog/README.md`, `pitfalls/README.md` from
67	   `assets/*.template`, substituting placeholders.
68	2. Appends an agent-guidance snippet to `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md` (auto-detected,
69	   override with `--agent-contract`).
70	3. Appends a "Roadmap & lessons learned" section to `README.md`.
71	4. Runs `scripts/todo-kanban.sh --validate-only TODO.md` so any drift is
72	   caught immediately.
73	5. Prints the deployment-exclusion lines you should add manually (it does
74	   not edit ignore files — see
75	   [`references/deployment-exclusion.md`](references/deployment-exclusion.md)).
76	
77	`init.sh` is idempotent: existing files are skipped unless `--force` is
78	given, and snippets append only if a sentinel marker is missing.
79	
80	### 2. Mid-conversation, when the user surfaces a "maybe later" idea
81	
82	Signals: "maybe later", "nice to have", "if I'm interested",
83	"工程量太大需要再評估", "先記下來", "not now but…".
84	
85	1. If `TODO.md` doesn't exist yet, run `scripts/init.sh` first.
86	2. **Default path — call `scripts/add-todo.sh`** with the priority,
87	   effort, title, and description. This inserts the canonical line into
88	   the right `## P*` lane and re-validates. Add `--backlog` if the
89	   conversation produced enough investigation that a `backlog/<slug>.md`
90	   doc is worth scaffolding.
91	
92	   ```sh
93	   scripts/add-todo.sh --priority "P?" --effort M \
94	     --title "Try Rspress for docs" \
95	     --description "Evaluate AI-native docs framework alternative"
96	   ```
97	
98	3. **Quick-capture path — append to `backlog/inbox.md`** when the user
99	   isn't sure of priority/effort yet, or is mid-thought:
100	
101	   ```sh
102	   echo "- $UNSTRUCTURED_THOUGHT" >> backlog/inbox.md
103	   ```
104	
105	   Later (this session or next), run `scripts/sweep-inbox.sh` to
106	   formalize the loose lines into `TODO.md` one at a time. The sweeper
107	   prompts for missing fields per line; in `--batch` mode it only
108	   processes lines that already have `priority=… effort=… title="…"
109	   description="…"` pairs and leaves ambiguous ones in place.
110	
111	4. **Manual edit path — only when scripts can't help.** Use the syntax
112	   from [`references/tag-schema.md`](references/tag-schema.md) and run
113	   `scripts/todo-kanban.sh --validate-only` afterwards.
114	
115	5. If you wrote a `backlog/<slug>.md` (either via `--backlog` or by
116	   hand), make sure the TODO line ends with
117	   ` → [research](backlog/<slug>.md)` so the index points to the doc.
118	
119	### 3. Mid-conversation, when you finish debugging something tricky
120	
121	Signals: "phew, that took a while", "weird, the error didn't say anything
122	about X", "this is the third time we've hit this", or you find yourself
123	reconstructing context that isn't in any doc.
124	
125	1. Create `pitfalls/<symptom-slug>.md` immediately from
126	   `assets/pitfall-doc.md.template`, while the trace is fresh. Title the
127	   doc by the **symptom**, not the root cause — you'll search by what
128	   you're seeing, not by what you eventually learned.
129	2. Copy verbatim error messages — never paraphrase, it kills grep-ability.
130	3. If the trap is severe (silent corruption / cross-machine recurrence /
131	   non-obvious workaround), surface it: "should this graduate to a Hard
132	   invariant in AGENTS.md?" — see
133	   [`references/when-to-add-docs.md`](references/when-to-add-docs.md).
134	
135	### 4. When implementing a `TODO.md` item
136	
137	In the same commit:
138	
139	1. Run `scripts/promote-todo.sh --title "<substring>" --summary "<what shipped>"`.
140	   It removes the active line and inserts the dated `Done` entry, then
141	   re-validates. It refuses to run if the substring matches zero or more
142	   than one active item.
143	2. If a `backlog/<slug>.md` exists, set its `Status: shipped` (don't
144	   delete — historical record may inform adjacent decisions).
145	3. If shipping uncovered a trap, write a `pitfalls/<slug>.md` for it.
146	
147	## When a TODO entry needs a `backlog/` doc, when a debug needs a `pitfalls/` doc
148	
149	Decision rules and the upgrade path to `AGENTS.md` invariants live in
150	[`references/when-to-add-docs.md`](references/when-to-add-docs.md). Read it
151	the first time you set up the harness; consult it again whenever you're
152	unsure which surface a piece of knowledge belongs in.
153	
154	## Tag schema
155	
156	Two orthogonal axes, validated by `scripts/todo-kanban.sh`. See
157	[`references/tag-schema.md`](references/tag-schema.md) for the full schema,
158	useful tag combinations, and the exact validator-checked syntax.
159	
160	## Anti-patterns
161	
162	Common mistakes to avoid (e.g., spawning `IDEAS.md` alongside `TODO.md`,
163	titling pitfalls by root cause, paraphrasing errors). Full list in
164	[`references/anti-patterns.md`](references/anti-patterns.md).
165	
166	## Deployment exclusion
167	
168	`TODO.md`, `backlog/`, and `pitfalls/` are maintainer-facing repo metadata,
169	not files to ship. Cheatsheet for chezmoi / npm / pip / Docker in
170	[`references/deployment-exclusion.md`](references/deployment-exclusion.md).
171	`scripts/init.sh --deployment ...` prints the exact lines to add.
172	
173	## Templates and bundled assets
174	
175	- `assets/TODO.md.template` — `TODO.md` skeleton with example items per lane
176	- `assets/backlog-README.md.template` — `backlog/` index + when-to-add rules
177	- `assets/backlog-doc.md.template` — single backlog doc (context-first)
178	- `assets/pitfalls-README.md.template` — `pitfalls/` index + cross-reference
179	  table for traps documented elsewhere
180	- `assets/pitfall-doc.md.template` — single pitfall doc (symptom-first)
181	- `assets/agent-guidance.md.template` — snippet for `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md`
182	- `assets/readme-roadmap.md.template` — snippet for project `README.md`
183	- `scripts/init.sh` — one-shot setup
184	- `scripts/todo-kanban.sh` — validator + Markdown kanban renderer
185	  (also supports `--json` and `--validate-only`)
186	- `scripts/add-todo.sh` — structured insert into `## P*` lane;
187	  `--backlog` also scaffolds `backlog/<slug>.md`
188	- `scripts/promote-todo.sh` — atomic active-→-Done move with re-validation
189	- `scripts/sweep-inbox.sh` — triage `backlog/inbox.md` → `add-todo.sh`
190	
191	## Reference implementation
192	
193	A live example of this harness is at
194	[`daviddwlee84/dotfiles`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles):
195	
196	- `TODO.md`, `backlog/`, `pitfalls/` directories at repo root
197	- `AGENTS.md` `### Long-term backlog → TODO.md + backlog/` and
198	  `### Past pitfalls → pitfalls/` sections
199	- `README.md` `## Roadmap & lessons learned` section

```text
1	---
2	name: skill-author
3	description: Author a new agent skill or refactor an existing one to follow agentskills.io best practices — gotchas sections, output templates, validation loops, calibrated specificity (fragility-based), and agentic script design (--help, --dry-run, structured stdout, stderr diagnostics, PEP 723 inline deps, pinned uvx/npx versions). Use whenever the user wants to create a new skill from scratch, scaffold a SKILL.md, write a reference file, design a script meant to be invoked by an agent, lint a draft skill for quality, or convert an ad-hoc workflow into a reusable skill. For evaluating skill output quality with test cases, benchmarking, or optimizing the description trigger rate, defer to the `skill-creator` skill instead — this skill focuses on authoring, not evaluation.
4	---
5	
6	# Skill Author
7	
8	Helps you write **new agent skills** that follow the best-practices documented at
9	https://agentskills.io/skill-creation/ — without you having to re-read those pages
10	every time. Pairs with `skill-creator` (which handles eval/iterate/optimize loops
11	once a draft exists).
12	
13	## When to use this vs `skill-creator`
14	
15	| Task | Use |
16	|---|---|
17	| "I want to make a new skill for X" | **skill-author** (scaffold + author) |
18	| "Scaffold the SKILL.md / a reference / a script" | **skill-author** |
19	| "Lint this skill draft" | **skill-author** |
20	| "My skill isn't triggering when I want it to" | `skill-creator` (description optimization) |
21	| "Run test cases against my skill, benchmark it" | `skill-creator` (eval loop) |
22	| "Compare two versions of my skill" | `skill-creator` (blind comparison) |
23	
24	If both apply, start here, then hand off to `skill-creator` once the draft is solid.
25	
26	## Workflow
27	
28	### 1. Capture intent (1 minute)
29	
30	Before scaffolding, get four answers — usually just by asking the user:
31	
32	1. **What does it do?** (one sentence)
33	2. **When should it trigger?** (specific user phrases / contexts)
34	3. **What does it output?** (file, command result, plan, prose)
35	4. **Is the output objectively verifiable?** (decides whether `skill-creator` evals are worth the effort later)
36	
37	Write these four down before touching files. They become the seeds for the
38	description, the workflow body, and the future eval set.
39	
40	### 2. Scaffold
41	
42	Use `scripts/new-skill.sh` to produce the directory layout:
43	
44	```bash
45	bash skills/local/skill-author/scripts/new-skill.sh <skill-name>
46	# creates: skills/local/<skill-name>/{SKILL.md,references/,scripts/,assets/}
47	# seeds:   SKILL.md from assets/SKILL.md.template
48	```
49	
50	The template's frontmatter has placeholders that lint will reject — this is on
51	purpose so the agent can't forget to fill them in.
52	
53	### 3. Author the SKILL.md
54	
55	Read `references/authoring-patterns.md` before writing the body. The patterns
56	that matter most:
57	
58	- **Description must be "pushy"** and include concrete trigger contexts. Naive
59	  descriptions cause undertriggering — the #1 failure mode of new skills.
60	- **Gotchas section** — environment-specific facts that defy reasonable
61	  assumptions. The single highest-value section in most skills.
62	- **Output templates** — agents pattern-match against concrete structures more
63	  reliably than they follow prose descriptions of formats.
64	- **Calibrated specificity** — be prescriptive only where the task is fragile;
65	  give the agent freedom (and explain *why*) where multiple approaches are valid.
66	- **Defaults, not menus** — pick one tool/approach and mention alternatives as
67	  escape hatches.
68	
69	Keep `SKILL.md` under 500 lines. If you blow past that, move detail into
70	`references/<topic>.md` and tell the agent **when** to load it ("Read X if Y
71	happens"), not just that it exists.
72	
73	### 4. Design any scripts
74	
75	Before writing a script, read `references/script-design.md`. Skills script
76	design is meaningfully different from "regular" CLI script design because the
77	caller is an LLM reading your stderr to decide what to do next. The non-obvious
78	requirements:
79	
80	- No interactive prompts, ever (agents run in non-interactive shells)
81	- `--help` is the primary interface documentation — keep it concise but complete
82	- Errors must say *what was expected* and *what to try*, not just *what failed*
83	- Structured stdout (JSON/CSV/TSV), prose diagnostics to stderr — separate them
84	- `--dry-run` for any destructive operation
85	- Pin versions for `uvx` / `npx` / `pipx` invocations
86	
87	For Python helpers, prefer **PEP 723 inline dependencies** + `uv run` over
88	`requirements.txt` — the script becomes self-contained and the agent doesn't
89	have to set up an environment first.
90	
91	### 5. Lint
92	
93	Run the linter before committing or handing off to `skill-creator`:
94	
95	```bash
96	bash skills/local/skill-author/scripts/lint-skill.sh skills/local/<skill-name>
97	```
98	
99	It checks three things:
100	
101	1. **Frontmatter & length** — `name` and `description` exist; description has a
102	   "use when" trigger phrase; SKILL.md is under 500 lines.
103	2. **Script hygiene** — every `scripts/*.sh` has a shebang, is executable, and
104	   responds to `--help` (presence of the flag handler, not necessarily a working
105	   script).
106	3. **Reference reachability** — every file in `references/` is mentioned at
107	   least once from `SKILL.md` (no dead reference docs).
108	
109	Fix every error. Warnings are advisory but usually worth addressing.
110	
111	### 6. (Optional) Hand off to skill-creator
112	
113	Once lint passes and the skill *looks* right, the next questions are
114	quantitative: does it trigger reliably? does it produce good output? That's
115	`skill-creator` territory. Tell the user: "skill-author got the structure
116	right. If you want to validate it works on real prompts, the `skill-creator`
117	skill runs test cases and benchmarks."
118	
119	## Available scripts
120	
121	- **`scripts/new-skill.sh <name>`** — Scaffold `skills/local/<name>/` with
122	  SKILL.md, references/, scripts/, assets/ from templates.
123	  - Flags: `--vendor` (use `skills/vendor/<name>/` instead — rare, normally
124	    vendored skills come via `vendor.yaml`); `--dry-run`; `--force` (overwrite
125	    existing).
126	- **`scripts/lint-skill.sh <skill-dir>`** — Run frontmatter, script hygiene,
127	  and reference reachability checks. Exit non-zero on any error.
128	  - Flags: `--strict` (treat warnings as errors); `--quiet` (only print failures).
129	
130	## Bundled assets
131	
132	Templates that `new-skill.sh` copies and that you can reference manually:
133	
134	- `assets/SKILL.md.template` — Frontmatter + workflow skeleton with placeholders.
135	- `assets/reference.md.template` — Reference doc skeleton (TOC + sections).
136	- `assets/script-bash.template` — Bash 3.2 compatible script with `set -euo pipefail`,
137	  `--help` / `--dry-run` flag handler, structured-output friendly logging
138	  (data → stdout, prose → stderr).
139	- `assets/script-python.template` — Python script with PEP 723 inline-deps
140	  block, argparse with help/examples, dry-run support.
141	
142	## Reference files
143	
144	- `references/authoring-patterns.md` — The agentskills.io "best practices"
145	  page condensed: gotchas, templates, validation loops, calibrated specificity,
146	  defaults-not-menus, procedures-over-declarations, plan-validate-execute.
147	- `references/script-design.md` — The agentskills.io "using scripts" page
148	  condensed: agentic CLI design, structured output, error message style,
149	  PEP 723, uvx/npx/pipx version pinning, dry-run patterns.
150	- `references/this-repo-conventions.md` — Conventions specific to *this*
151	  repository: where to put local vs vendor skills, how the 5-level skill
152	  search works, AGENTS.md ↔ CLAUDE.md sync, where mirrored scripts live.
153	
154	## Gotchas
155	
156	- **AGENTS.md is a symlink to CLAUDE.md** — edit either one; never replace the
157	  symlink with a real file.
158	- **Skill discovery is one level deep first, then recursive up to 5 levels.**
159	  `skills/local/<name>/SKILL.md` works because of the recursive fallback. Don't
160	  nest skills more than 5 deep or they become invisible.
161	- **`bash 3.2` compatibility** is required for any script that might run on
162	  stock macOS. No `mapfile`, no `${var,,}` lowercasing, no `[[ -v var ]]`.
163	  See `references/script-design.md` for the safe subset.
164	- **`description` field length matters less than its trigger surface area.**
165	  A 200-word description that names 8 concrete contexts will outperform a
166	  50-word one that's beautifully concise but vague. Err on the side of more
167	  trigger phrases.
168	- **Don't write a skill that wraps something the agent already does well.**
169	  If a stock Claude session handles the task in one turn without help, a skill
170	  adds context-window cost for no gain. Test the no-skill baseline before
171	  investing in authoring.
172	
173	## When the user is updating an existing skill (not creating new)
174	
175	Same workflow, but skip step 2 (scaffold). Read the existing SKILL.md first,
176	identify which patterns from `references/authoring-patterns.md` are missing or
177	weakly applied, and propose edits one section at a time so the user can sanity
178	check. After edits, run lint, then offer the `skill-creator` handoff for
179	quantitative validation.
180

Research complete. Plan written to `/Users/daviddwlee84/.claude/plans/skill-agent-history-specstory-skill-proud-sedgewick-agent-a0fc59f42c3978828.md`. Summary of key findings:

## 1. SpecStory
- **Files land at:** `.specstory/history/*.md` — one timestamp-named Markdown per session. Also `.specstory/ai_rules_backups/` (auto-gitignored by SpecStory itself).
- **CLI:** `brew install specstory`. Key commands: `specstory run claude`, `specstory watch`, `specstory list claude`, `specstory sync claude -s <uuid>`.
- **Config (TOML):** `~/.specstory/cli/config.toml` (user) and `.specstory/cli/config.toml` (project). VS Code extension adds `specstory.autoSave`.
- **Active session:** No first-class selector. Heuristic: find the most-recently-modified `~/.claude/projects/<cwd-slug>/<uuid>.jsonl`, feed that UUID to `specstory sync claude -s <uuid>`. Alternative: newest mtime in `.specstory/history/`.
- **`.gitignore` guidance:** Official doc says **commit** `.specstory/history/` alongside code — do not ignore.

## 2. Claude Code `plansDirectory`
- Confirmed valid key in `.claude/settings.json`. Default is `~/.claude/plans/`.
- **Works at both user and project level** (standard precedence: local > project > user). Setting it user-level does globally force a destination across every repo; setting it to `".claude/plans"` project-level is the canonical way to commit plans with code.
- **Caveat:** [issue #19537](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/19537) reports project-level value being ignored in some versions — the skill should verify where the plan file actually landed, not trust the config.

## 3. Gitleaks
- **Staged scan:** `gitleaks protect --staged --redact` (deprecated since v8.19.0 → prefer `gitleaks git --staged --redact`).
- **Global hook:** `git config --global core.hooksPath ~/.config/git/hooks` with a `pre-commit` script calling gitleaks. Preferable to `init.templateDir` because it applies to already-cloned repos. Hook should support `SKIP=gitleaks` and soft-fail if the binary is absent.
- **SpecStory gotcha:** Transcripts echo example keys (`sk-...`, `ghp_...`, fake AKIA). Add a `.gitleaks.toml` allowlist for `.specstory/history/.*\.md` and `.claude/plans/.*\.md`. Performance-wise `--staged` only scans the diff, so normal commits are cheap; the first bulk commit of history is the expensive one.

## 4. Accidentally committed a secret
Canonical advice (avoids force-push reflex):
1. **Rotate immediately** at the provider — the only step that actually protects you.
2. **Remove from HEAD** and push a follow-up commit.
3. **Rewrite history only if cheap** (solo branch, not yet shared). Use `git filter-repo --invert-paths --path <file>` or BFG; on a shared branch this risks recontamination from stale teammate clones.
4. On GitHub, enable push protection / secret scanning and ask Support to purge cached views if needed.

Tagline for the skill: **"Rotate first. Scrub second, only if cheap. Never rely on rewriting history to keep a secret secret."**

6	# DVC ML Workflow
7	
8	DVC turns a git repo into a full ML lab: data and model files are versioned out-of-band (in a cache + remote), pipelines are declared in `dvc.yaml`, and experiments are run as ephemeral git commits with metrics and plots attached. No tracking server, no separate database — everything lives in your existing git history.
9	
10	This skill is opinionated about **the parts of DVC that matter for production ML work**: pipelines, queued experiments, metrics/commit binding, and remotes. It defers to the official docs at https://dvc.org/doc for everything else and links them inline so the agent always pulls the latest guidance.
11	
12	## When to use
13	
14	- User wants reproducible ML pipelines without a tracking server (`mlflow`, `wandb`, etc.)
15	- User mentions `dvc.yaml`, `params.yaml`, `dvc exp run`, `dvc queue`, `dvc push`, `.dvc/cache`
16	- User wants to do a hyperparameter sweep / grid search and have each run land as a separate commit with metrics
17	- User wants to version a dataset or model file too large for git
18	- User asks "how do I make my training reproducible" and is already on git
19	- User wants `mlflow ui`-style experiment comparison but **doesn't want to run a server** (DVC's `dvc exp show` + VS Code extension fills that role)
20	
21	## When NOT to use
22	
23	- User wants a hosted experiment dashboard with multi-user collaboration → use `mlflow-tracking` skill
24	- User wants LLM trace observability (spans, prompts, token costs) → DVC has no story here; use `mlflow-tracking`
25	- User just needs `git lfs` for a few large files → DVC is overkill; recommend `git lfs`
26	- User has an existing `mlflow` workflow and is happy with it → don't push DVC unless they ask
27	
28	## Authoritative sources (always link these, don't paraphrase from memory)
29	
30	- Docs root: https://dvc.org/doc
31	- Command reference: https://dvc.org/doc/command-reference
32	- User guide: https://dvc.org/doc/user-guide
33	- Upstream repo: https://github.com/treeverse/dvc (formerly `iterative/dvc`; redirects)
34	- PyPI: https://pypi.org/project/dvc/
35	
36	When you're unsure of a flag, syntax, or behavior, **fetch the relevant doc page** rather than guessing — DVC's CLI surface changes between minor versions.
37	
38	## Core mental model
39	
40	Three orthogonal things, often confused:
41	
42	| DVC concept | Analogy | What it does |
43	|---|---|---|
44	| `dvc add <file>` | `git lfs track` | Snapshots a single file/dir into the cache, writes a `.dvc` pointer file (which **is** committed to git) |
45	| `dvc.yaml` (stages) | `Makefile` | Declares pipeline stages with dependencies and outputs; `dvc repro` re-runs only stages whose inputs changed |
46	| `dvc exp run` | `git commit` for experiments | Runs the pipeline once with optional param overrides, captures metrics + outputs as an **ephemeral commit** |
47	
48	The non-obvious bit: `dvc exp run` builds on top of `dvc.yaml`. You don't choose between "use pipelines" and "run experiments" — you write the pipeline once, then launch many experiments against it.
49	
50	## Workflow

5	
6	# Skill Author
7	
8	Helps you write **new agent skills** that follow the best-practices documented at
9	https://agentskills.io/skill-creation/ — without you having to re-read those pages
10	every time. Pairs with `skill-creator` (which handles eval/iterate/optimize loops
11	once a draft exists).
12	
13	## When to use this vs `skill-creator`
14	
15	| Task | Use |
16	|---|---|
17	| "I want to make a new skill for X" | **skill-author** (scaffold + author) |
18	| "Scaffold the SKILL.md / a reference / a script" | **skill-author** |
19	| "Lint this skill draft" | **skill-author** |
20	| "My skill isn't triggering when I want it to" | `skill-creator` (description optimization) |
21	| "Run test cases against my skill, benchmark it" | `skill-creator` (eval loop) |
22	| "Compare two versions of my skill" | `skill-creator` (blind comparison) |
23	
24	If both apply, start here, then hand off to `skill-creator` once the draft is solid.
25	
26	## Workflow
27	
28	### 1. Capture intent (1 minute)
29	
30	Before scaffolding, get four answers — usually just by asking the user:
31	
32	1. **What does it do?** (one sentence)
33	2. **When should it trigger?** (specific user phrases / contexts)
34	3. **What does it output?** (file, command result, plan, prose)
35	4. **Is the output objectively verifiable?** (decides whether `skill-creator` evals are worth the effort later)
36	
37	Write these four down before touching files. They become the seeds for the
38	description, the workflow body, and the future eval set.
39	
40	### 2. Scaffold
41	
42	Use `scripts/new-skill.sh` to produce the directory layout:
43	
44	```bash
45	bash skills/local/skill-author/scripts/new-skill.sh <skill-name>
46	# creates: skills/local/<skill-name>/{SKILL.md,references/,scripts/,assets/}
47	# seeds:   SKILL.md from assets/SKILL.md.template
48	```
49	
50	The template's frontmatter has placeholders that lint will reject — this is on
51	purpose so the agent can't forget to fill them in.
52	
53	### 3. Author the SKILL.md
54	
55	Read `references/authoring-patterns.md` before writing the body. The patterns
56	that matter most:
57	
58	- **Description must be "pushy"** and include concrete trigger contexts. Naive
59	  descriptions cause undertriggering — the #1 failure mode of new skills.
60	- **Gotchas section** — environment-specific facts that defy reasonable
61	  assumptions. The single highest-value section in most skills.
62	- **Output templates** — agents pattern-match against concrete structures more
63	  reliably than they follow prose descriptions of formats.
64	- **Calibrated specificity** — be prescriptive only where the task is fragile;
65	  give the agent freedom (and explain *why*) where multiple approaches are valid.
66	- **Defaults, not menus** — pick one tool/approach and mention alternatives as
67	  escape hatches.
68	
69	Keep `SKILL.md` under 500 lines. If you blow past that, move detail into
70	`references/<topic>.md` and tell the agent **when** to load it ("Read X if Y
71	happens"), not just that it exists.
72	
73	### 4. Design any scripts
74	
75	Before writing a script, read `references/script-design.md`. Skills script
76	design is meaningfully different from "regular" CLI script design because the
77	caller is an LLM reading your stderr to decide what to do next. The non-obvious
78	requirements:
79	
80	- No interactive prompts, ever (agents run in non-interactive shells)

6	# project-knowledge-harness
7	
8	A lightweight, file-based memory harness for any software project.
9	
10	Three surfaces, sharply separated by **time direction** and **access pattern**:
11	
12	| Surface | Time | Question it answers | Access pattern |
13	|---|---|---|---|
14	| `TODO.md` | Future | "What might we do later?" | Read top to bottom (priority lanes) |
15	| `backlog/<slug>.md` | Future | "What was the analysis behind this idea?" | Indexed from `TODO.md` |
16	| `pitfalls/<slug>.md` | **Past** | **"I see error X — has this happened before?"** | **Grep symptom keywords** |
17	
18	Plus, in projects that already have agent contracts, `AGENTS.md` Hard
19	invariants answer "What rules MUST agents follow?". Pitfalls *graduate* to
20	Hard invariants when serious enough — see
21	[`references/when-to-add-docs.md`](references/when-to-add-docs.md).
22	
23	## When to use this skill
24	
25	Use this skill when the user surfaces any of:
26	
27	- A long-term TODO list with no home, or a messy `TODO.md` that needs
28	  structure (signals: "where should ideas go?", "maybe later", "工程量太大需要再評估")
29	- A debugging session worth saving (signals: "keep solving the same problem
30	  twice", "save this troubleshooting", "踩過的坑", "TROUBLESHOOTING.md
31	  scattered across docs/")
32	- A request to consolidate `IDEAS.md` / `ROADMAP.md` / `WISHLIST.md` /
33	  `LESSONS.md` files
34	
35	Do NOT use this skill for active sprint planning (use issue trackers),
36	ephemeral agent scratchpads (use `.claude/plans/`), or current feature
37	documentation (use `docs/`).
38

1	# Dotfiles Repository — Agent Contract
2	
3	Cross-platform dotfiles managed by **chezmoi** (configs) + **ansible** (system deps). This file is the agent-facing contract: maintenance rules, hard invariants, and pointers to docs. User-facing intro is in [README.md](README.md).
4	
5	> **Headroom rule**: keep this file under ~30k chars. Push handbook content into `docs/`; keep only edit rules and cross-file invariants here.
6	
7	## Cross-file maintenance rules
8	
9	When you change one of these surfaces, update the listed mirror file in the same commit. These are the rules most often forgotten.
10	
11	### README.md
12	
13	When adding/modifying configurations, update [README.md](README.md):
14	
15	- **New config files** → "What You Get > Config Files" section
16	- **New ansible roles/tools** → "What You Get > Tools" section
17	- **New platforms** → "Supported Platforms" table
18	- **Changed setup steps** → "Quick Setup" section
19	
20	Keep README.md concise and user-focused. Technical details belong here or in `docs/`.
21	
22	### Custom aliases & shell functions → `docs/zsh/aliases.md`
23	
24	When adding/modifying/removing a custom alias or shell function in any `dot_config/zsh/` file, update [`docs/zsh/aliases.md`](docs/zsh/aliases.md): one row per entry with command name, type (`alias` or `function`), source file (relative to repo root), and a one-line description.
25	
26	### Dockerfile + dotfiles_init wrapper
27	
28	When adding new chezmoi prompts in `.chezmoi.toml.tmpl`, three files must be updated in the same commit:
29	
30	1. `Dockerfile` — add `ARG CHEZMOI_*` build argument, add `--promptBool` / `--promptString` flag to `chezmoi init`.
31	2. `scripts/init/dotfiles_init.py` — add a matching entry to the `PROMPTS` tuple (key, kind, group, label, desc, default).
32	3. (If the prompt should be part of any named bundle) `BUNDLES` dict in the same file.
33	
34	Verify parity with: `uv run --script scripts/init/dotfiles_init.py doctor`. The subcommand greps `.chezmoi.toml.tmpl` + `Dockerfile` and compares against the embedded `PROMPTS`; non-zero exit means drift.
35	
36	### Agent artifact redaction
37	
38	SpecStory transcripts and coding-agent plan files commonly paste shell output, config snippets, or `.env` values that may contain secrets. Four directories are auto-scanned/redacted:
39	
40	| Prefix | Source |
41	|--------|--------|
42	| `.specstory/history/` | SpecStory chat transcripts |
43	| `.claude/plans/` | Claude Code plan files |
44	| `.cursor/plans/` | Cursor plan files |
45	| `.opencode/plans/` | OpenCode plan files |
46	
47	Tooling: `scripts/redact_secrets.py` (gitleaks + `PRIV***KEY` pattern), `just check-secrets` / `just redact-secrets` / `just add-and-redact`. Pre-commit hook `redact-agent-secrets` runs `--fix` before `gitleaks-system`; if it rewrites a file, stage and retry.
48	
49	When introducing a new coding-agent artifact directory that could contain secrets, add its prefix to `DEFAULT_PATHS` in `scripts/redact_secrets.py` **and** the `files:` regex of the `redact-agent-secrets` pre-commit hook.
50	
51	### Keyboard shortcuts (cross-tool conflict check)
52	
53	When adding/modifying keybindings in any tool config, cross-check against other tools — multiple tools share the terminal's key namespace, especially `Ctrl+` and `Alt+`.
54	
55	| Tool | Config file | Conflict risk |
56	|------|-------------|---------------|
57	| tmux (root-table) | `dot_config/tmux/keybindings.conf` | `C-h/j/k/l` (vim-tmux-navigator), `C-1..9` (window switch) |
58	| Television (global) | `dot_config/television/config.toml` | `Ctrl+S/F/R/Y/T/X/O` (built-in actions) |
59	| Television (channels) | `dot_config/television/cable/*.toml` | Per-channel `[keybindings]` overrides global |
60	| Zellij | `dot_config/zellij/config.kdl` | Mitigated by `default_mode "locked"` |
61	| Ghostty | `dot_config/ghostty/config` | `macos-option-as-alt` affects `Alt+` availability |
62	
63	Known conflict zones: `Ctrl+H/J/K/L` (tmux vim-tmux-navigator; removed in TV global), `Ctrl+S/F/R` (TV built-in cycling/reload — avoid in channel actions), `Alt+*` (safe namespace for channel-specific actions; requires terminal to send Option as Meta).
64	
65	**Resolution precedence**: tmux root-table bindings intercept keys before they reach the inner application. Inside tmux, any `bind-key -n C-*` shadows the same `ctrl-*` in TV. Prefer `Alt+` for custom actions.
66	
67	### Long-term backlog + past pitfalls → use the `project-knowledge-harness` skill
68	
69	This repo uses the `project-knowledge-harness` agent skill (managed via
70	`~/.agents/.skill-lock.json` → restored by
71	`run_onchange_after_40_install_global_skills.sh.tmpl` on every `chezmoi apply`;
72	see [docs/tools/agent-skills.md](docs/tools/agent-skills.md)). **Load the skill**
73	for the full template, disambiguation table, and upgrade path.

75	**Fallback (if the skill cannot be loaded)** — minimum viable rules so this

78	- Three repo-root surfaces, all `chezmoi`-ignored, all NOT auto-redacted:
79	  [`TODO.md`](TODO.md) (priority/effort tags `P1`/`P2`/`P3`/`P?` × `S`/`M`/`L`/`XL`),
80	  [`backlog/`](backlog/README.md) (research/design notes; needed for `P?` /
81	  `[L]` / `[XL]` / multi-option entries), [`pitfalls/`](pitfalls/README.md)
82	  (debugged traps, **titled by symptom not root cause**, verbatim error
83	  messages — never paraphrase).
84	- Triggers to capture future work: "maybe later", "nice to have", "if I'm
85	  interested", "工程量太大需要再評估", "先記下來".
86	- Triggers to capture pitfalls: >~15 min debugging, not googleable,
87	  non-obvious fix, silent failure mode.
88	- Do **not** spawn `ROADMAP.md` / `IDEAS.md` / `LESSONS.md` /
89	  `TROUBLESHOOTING.md` — three surfaces, always.

91	  across machines, (b) silently corrupts state, or (c) has a non-obvious

Based on the search results, here's what I found about SpecStory's chat history storage:

## Storage Location
SpecStory saves every AI interaction locally to .specstory/history/ in your project.

## File Format
Each conversation is stored as a separate Markdown file. More specifically, inside the .specstory/history/ directory, you should see a Markdown file of your session, named with a timestamp.

## How It Works
The SpecStory CLI auto-generates markdown files from your chat sessions with terminal agents (e.g. Claude Code, Cursor CLI, Codex CLI, Droid CLI, Gemini CLI, etc.) and saves your conversations to .specstory/history/ in your project.

So in summary, the filename format uses timestamps for naming the individual markdown files within the `.specstory/history/` folder, making each conversation easily identifiable by when it was created.

Based on the search results, here's what I found about the `plansDirectory` setting in Claude Code's `.claude/settings.json` and Plan Mode:

## Overview

The plansDirectory setting specifies where Claude Code stores plan files generated during Plan Mode sessions. By default, plan files are stored in ~/.claude/plans/, but this setting lets you customize the storage location.

## Configuration

plansDirectory: Change where plan files are stored. You can add this to your `.claude/settings.json` like so:

```json
{
  "plansDirectory": "./plans"
}
```

## Project-Local vs Global

If you want plans stored inside your project for version control, set plansDirectory in settings.json to a project-relative path like ./plans. Project-relative plans open up workflows that ~/.claude/plans/ can't support: Review plan diffs in pull requests before anyone starts coding · Carry annotations forward across sessions without relying on context compaction · Treat the markdown file as a living spec that multiple team members edit directly.

## Known Issue

The plansDirectory setting in a project's .claude/settings.json is being ignored. Instead, Claude Code uses the global default path (~/.claude/plans/). This appears to be a reported bug in some versions of Claude Code.

Based on the search results, here's what I found about using `gitleaks protect --staged` with pre-commit hooks and the global `core.hooksPath`:

## Key Concepts

**gitleaks protect --staged**: This command scans staged changes to ensure no secrets (e.g., API keys) are committed.

**Pre-commit Hooks**: Pre-commit hooks are scripts that run automatically before a commit is finalized within a Git repository and are configured within the repository's .git/hooks directory or managed using tools like pre-commit.

**Global core.hooksPath Configuration**: After install, Git will use a global hooks directory with hooks living at `~/.config/git/hooks/` with `pre-commit` scanning staged changes, and Git is set to use it globally via `git config --global core.hooksPath ~/.config/git/hooks`.

## Setting Up a Global Pre-commit Hook

You can edit your global git config file (usually .gitconfig in your home) to add the core.hooksPath configuration like `[core] hooksPath = /home/<your_user>/gitconfig/hooks`.

A pre-commit hook script can use `gitleaks protect -c <path_to_custom_Gitleaks_rules> -v --staged --redact` to scan for secrets before committing.

A simple bash hook can use `gitleaks protect --staged --redact` to check staged changes, and you can prepend SKIP=gitleaks to the commit command to skip the gitleaks check if needed.

I found comprehensive information about remediating accidentally committed secrets in Git repositories. Here are the key findings:

## Immediate Actions

Once a secret's been committed, assume it's compromised and rotate it right away, revoking any old tokens or credentials.

## Tools for Removing Secrets from History

**git-filter-repo** (Recommended Modern Tool):
git-filter-repo is the modern, fast, and officially recommended tool for rewriting Git history (it replaces the older git filter-branch). The --invert-paths flag deletes the file (or files) from every commit, ensuring no historical trace remains.

**BFG Repo-Cleaner** (Alternative):
BFG is a tool that allows you to scrub your git repositories clean and remove all sensitive data that you might have accidentally committed and luckily is extremely simple to use and extremely fast.

## The Process

You'll use a mirror clone — a minimal, metadata-rich copy of your repository — ideal for surgical operations.

Use the command to target the specific file containing the secret (e.g., git filter-repo --path path/to/secret/file --invert-paths). The tool will rewrite every commit in your history. If the file existed in 100 commits, all 100 commits will be modified to remove that file.

## Important Considerations

High risk of recontamination exists: if a fellow developer has a clone from before your rewrite, and after your rewrite simply runs git pull followed by git push, the sensitive data will return.

Once you've pushed to git, consider it compromised forever, particularly since anyone could have pulled it. Always reset/rotate secrets once you've made this mistake!
