5	
6	# Skill Author
7	
8	Helps you write **new agent skills** that follow the best-practices documented at
9	https://agentskills.io/skill-creation/ — without you having to re-read those pages
10	every time. Pairs with `skill-creator` (which handles eval/iterate/optimize loops
11	once a draft exists).
12	
13	## When to use this vs `skill-creator`
14	
15	| Task | Use |
16	|---|---|
17	| "I want to make a new skill for X" | **skill-author** (scaffold + author) |
18	| "Scaffold the SKILL.md / a reference / a script" | **skill-author** |
19	| "Lint this skill draft" | **skill-author** |
20	| "My skill isn't triggering when I want it to" | `skill-creator` (description optimization) |
21	| "Run test cases against my skill, benchmark it" | `skill-creator` (eval loop) |
22	| "Compare two versions of my skill" | `skill-creator` (blind comparison) |
23	
24	If both apply, start here, then hand off to `skill-creator` once the draft is solid.
25	
26	## Workflow
27	
28	### 1. Capture intent (1 minute)
29	
30	Before scaffolding, get four answers — usually just by asking the user:
31	
32	1. **What does it do?** (one sentence)
33	2. **When should it trigger?** (specific user phrases / contexts)
34	3. **What does it output?** (file, command result, plan, prose)
35	4. **Is the output objectively verifiable?** (decides whether `skill-creator` evals are worth the effort later)
36	
37	Write these four down before touching files. They become the seeds for the
38	description, the workflow body, and the future eval set.
39	
40	### 2. Scaffold
41	
42	Use `scripts/new-skill.sh` to produce the directory layout:
43	
44	```bash
45	bash skills/local/skill-author/scripts/new-skill.sh <skill-name>
46	# creates: skills/local/<skill-name>/{SKILL.md,references/,scripts/,assets/}
47	# seeds:   SKILL.md from assets/SKILL.md.template
48	```
49	
50	The template's frontmatter has placeholders that lint will reject — this is on
51	purpose so the agent can't forget to fill them in.
52	
53	### 3. Author the SKILL.md
54	
55	Read `references/authoring-patterns.md` before writing the body. The patterns
56	that matter most:
57	
58	- **Description must be "pushy"** and include concrete trigger contexts. Naive
59	  descriptions cause undertriggering — the #1 failure mode of new skills.
60	- **Gotchas section** — environment-specific facts that defy reasonable
61	  assumptions. The single highest-value section in most skills.
62	- **Output templates** — agents pattern-match against concrete structures more
63	  reliably than they follow prose descriptions of formats.
64	- **Calibrated specificity** — be prescriptive only where the task is fragile;
65	  give the agent freedom (and explain *why*) where multiple approaches are valid.
66	- **Defaults, not menus** — pick one tool/approach and mention alternatives as
67	  escape hatches.
68	
69	Keep `SKILL.md` under 500 lines. If you blow past that, move detail into
70	`references/<topic>.md` and tell the agent **when** to load it ("Read X if Y
71	happens"), not just that it exists.
72	
73	### 4. Design any scripts
74	
75	Before writing a script, read `references/script-design.md`. Skills script
76	design is meaningfully different from "regular" CLI script design because the
77	caller is an LLM reading your stderr to decide what to do next. The non-obvious
78	requirements:
79	
80	- No interactive prompts, ever (agents run in non-interactive shells)
81	- `--help` is the primary interface documentation — keep it concise but complete
82	- Errors must say *what was expected* and *what to try*, not just *what failed*
83	- Structured stdout (JSON/CSV/TSV), prose diagnostics to stderr — separate them
84	- `--dry-run` for any destructive operation
85	- Pin versions for `uvx` / `npx` / `pipx` invocations
86	
87	For Python helpers, prefer **PEP 723 inline dependencies** + `uv run` over
88	`requirements.txt` — the script becomes self-contained and the agent doesn't
89	have to set up an environment first.
90	
91	### 5. Lint
92	
93	Run the linter before committing or handing off to `skill-creator`:
94	
95	```bash
96	bash skills/local/skill-author/scripts/lint-skill.sh skills/local/<skill-name>
97	```
98	
99	It checks three things:
100	
101	1. **Frontmatter & length** — `name` and `description` exist; description has a
102	   "use when" trigger phrase; SKILL.md is under 500 lines.
103	2. **Script hygiene** — every `scripts/*.sh` has a shebang, is executable, and
104	   responds to `--help` (presence of the flag handler, not necessarily a working
105	   script).
106	3. **Reference reachability** — every file in `references/` is mentioned at
107	   least once from `SKILL.md` (no dead reference docs).
108	
109	Fix every error. Warnings are advisory but usually worth addressing.
110	
111	### 6. (Optional) Hand off to skill-creator
112	
113	Once lint passes and the skill *looks* right, the next questions are
114	quantitative: does it trigger reliably? does it produce good output? That's
115	`skill-creator` territory. Tell the user: "skill-author got the structure
116	right. If you want to validate it works on real prompts, the `skill-creator`
117	skill runs test cases and benchmarks."
118	
119	## Available scripts
120	
121	- **`scripts/new-skill.sh <name>`** — Scaffold `skills/local/<name>/` with
122	  SKILL.md, references/, scripts/, assets/ from templates.
123	  - Flags: `--vendor` (use `skills/vendor/<name>/` instead — rare, normally
124	    vendored skills come via `vendor.yaml`); `--dry-run`; `--force` (overwrite
125	    existing).
126	- **`scripts/lint-skill.sh <skill-dir>`** — Run frontmatter, script hygiene,
127	  and reference reachability checks. Exit non-zero on any error.
128	  - Flags: `--strict` (treat warnings as errors); `--quiet` (only print failures).
129	
130	## Bundled assets
131	
132	Templates that `new-skill.sh` copies and that you can reference manually:
133	
134	- `assets/SKILL.md.template` — Frontmatter + workflow skeleton with placeholders.
135	- `assets/reference.md.template` — Reference doc skeleton (TOC + sections).
136	- `assets/script-bash.template` — Bash 3.2 compatible script with `set -euo pipefail`,
137	  `--help` / `--dry-run` flag handler, structured-output friendly logging
138	  (data → stdout, prose → stderr).
139	- `assets/script-python.template` — Python script with PEP 723 inline-deps
140	  block, argparse with help/examples, dry-run support.
141	
142	## Reference files
143	
144	- `references/authoring-patterns.md` — The agentskills.io "best practices"
145	  page condensed: gotchas, templates, validation loops, calibrated specificity,
146	  defaults-not-menus, procedures-over-declarations, plan-validate-execute.
147	- `references/script-design.md` — The agentskills.io "using scripts" page
148	  condensed: agentic CLI design, structured output, error message style,
149	  PEP 723, uvx/npx/pipx version pinning, dry-run patterns.
150	- `references/this-repo-conventions.md` — Conventions specific to *this*
151	  repository: where to put local vs vendor skills, how the 5-level skill
152	  search works, AGENTS.md ↔ CLAUDE.md sync, where mirrored scripts live.
153	
154	## Gotchas
155	
156	- **AGENTS.md is a symlink to CLAUDE.md** — edit either one; never replace the
157	  symlink with a real file.
158	- **Skill discovery is one level deep first, then recursive up to 5 levels.**
159	  `skills/local/<name>/SKILL.md` works because of the recursive fallback. Don't
160	  nest skills more than 5 deep or they become invisible.
161	- **`bash 3.2` compatibility** is required for any script that might run on
162	  stock macOS. No `mapfile`, no `${var,,}` lowercasing, no `[[ -v var ]]`.
163	  See `references/script-design.md` for the safe subset.
164	- **`description` field length matters less than its trigger surface area.**
165	  A 200-word description that names 8 concrete contexts will outperform a
166	  50-word one that's beautifully concise but vague. Err on the side of more
167	  trigger phrases.
168	- **Don't write a skill that wraps something the agent already does well.**
169	  If a stock Claude session handles the task in one turn without help, a skill
170	  adds context-window cost for no gain. Test the no-skill baseline before
171	  investing in authoring.
172	
173	## When the user is updating an existing skill (not creating new)
174	
175	Same workflow, but skip step 2 (scaffold). Read the existing SKILL.md first,
176	identify which patterns from `references/authoring-patterns.md` are missing or

1	---
2	name: marimo-batch-mlflow
3	description: Prepare a marimo notebook to run as both an interactive UI and a scheduled batch script, using Tyro for CLI parsing (with dataclass or Pydantic params) and MLflow for experiment tracking. Use when the user wants the same marimo notebook to serve as both a UI for iteration and a CLI script for batch jobs / hyperparameter sweeps, and prefers Tyro over `mo.cli_args()` and MLflow over Weights and Biases. For the upstream W&B + `mo.cli_args()` variant, see marimo-team/skills/skills/marimo-batch.
4	---
5	
6	# marimo-batch-mlflow
7	
8	Opinionated fork of [marimo-team/skills/marimo-batch](https://github.com/marimo-team/skills/tree/main/skills/marimo-batch) that:
9	
10	1. Uses **[Tyro](https://brentyi.github.io/tyro/)** for CLI parsing (works with `dataclass`, `pydantic.BaseModel`, or `attrs`) instead of `mo.cli_args()` + manual help-table rendering.
11	2. Uses **[MLflow](https://mlflow.org/)** + **[mlflow-widgets](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/mlflow-widgets)** for experiment tracking instead of Weights and Biases.
12	3. Keeps the dual-mode pattern (`mo.app_meta().mode == "script"`) so a single `notebook.py` is both the UI for iteration and the entry point for `uv run notebook.py --epochs 50` batch jobs.
13	
14	## When to use this vs upstream `marimo-batch`
15	
16	| Concern | upstream `marimo-batch` | this skill |
17	|---|---|---|
18	| CLI parsing | `mo.cli_args()` + hand-rolled `rich.Table` for `--help` | `tyro.cli(ModelParams)` — auto `--help`, type coercion, validation |
19	| Params model | Pydantic `BaseModel` | `dataclass` (primary) or `pydantic.BaseModel` (alternative) |
20	| Tracking backend | Weights and Biases (`wandb`) | MLflow (`mlflow` + optional `mlflow-widgets` for live charts) |
21	| Live training UI | none — W&B web dashboard only | `mlflow_widgets.MlflowChart` cell, gated off in script mode |
22	| Grid launcher | HF Jobs + `WANDB_API_KEY` secret | HF Jobs + `MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI` (+ optional `MLFLOW_TRACKING_TOKEN`) |
23	
24	Pick this skill when the user has a self-hosted MLflow server (or local `./mlruns` is fine) and prefers strongly-typed CLIs. Pick upstream when the user is already on W&B.
25	
26	## Dual-mode pattern
27	
28	The single source-of-truth idiom: branch on `mo.app_meta().mode == "script"` once, build `params` either from a form or from CLI flags, then **let every downstream cell consume `params` regardless of source**.
29	
30	```python
31	import marimo as mo
32	
33	is_script_mode = mo.app_meta().mode == "script"
34	
35	if is_script_mode:
36	    params = tyro.cli(ModelParams)
37	else:
38	    mo.stop(form.value is None, mo.md("*Submit the form to start training.*"))
39	    params = ModelParams(**form.value)
40	
41	# Every cell below uses `params.epochs`, `params.batch_size`, ...
42	# unaware of which branch produced it.
43	```
44	
45	This is what makes the notebook usable as both a UI for fast iteration and a CLI script for sweeps without code duplication.
46	
47	## Params with dataclass + Tyro (primary)
48	
49	```python
50	from dataclasses import dataclass
51	import tyro
52	
53	@dataclass
54	class ModelParams:
55	    """Model training parameters."""
56	    epochs: int = 25
57	    """Number of training epochs."""
58	    batch_size: int = 32
59	    """Training batch size."""
60	    learning_rate: float = 1e-4
61	    """Learning rate for AdamW."""
62	    mlflow_experiment: str = "batch-sizes"
63	    """MLflow experiment name (empty string disables logging)."""
64	    mlflow_run_name: str | None = None
65	    """Optional explicit run name; auto-derived from params if None."""
66	
67	if is_script_mode:
68	    params = tyro.cli(ModelParams)
69	```
70	
71	Tyro derives `--epochs INT`, `--batch-size INT`, etc., from the field names; PEP 257 docstrings under each field become CLI help text. `--help` is generated automatically — no `rich.Table` boilerplate needed.
72	
73	CLI usage:
74	
75	```bash
76	uv run notebook.py --epochs 50 --batch-size 64 --learning-rate 5e-4
77	uv run notebook.py --help     # auto-generated
78	```
79	
80	## Params with Pydantic (alternative)
81	
82	Tyro v0.8+ supports `pydantic.BaseModel` directly. Trade `dataclass` for Pydantic when you need field-level validators or `@computed_field`:
83	
84	```python
85	from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
86	import tyro
87	
88	class ModelParams(BaseModel):
89	    epochs: int = Field(default=25, description="Number of training epochs.")
90	    batch_size: int = Field(default=32, description="Training batch size.")
91	    learning_rate: float = Field(default=1e-4, description="Learning rate.")
92	    mlflow_experiment: str = Field(default="batch-sizes")
93	
94	params = tyro.cli(ModelParams)  # same call site
95	```
96	
97	`Field(description=...)` becomes CLI help. See [`references/params-pydantic.py`](references/params-pydantic.py) for the cell-level diff against the dataclass version.
98	
99	## MLflow tracking
100	
101	Wrap the training loop in `mlflow.start_run()`. Default to graceful degradation when `MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI` is unset (MLflow falls back to `./mlruns/`). Disable logging entirely by setting `params.mlflow_experiment = ""`.
102	
103	```python
104	import mlflow
105	import os
106	
107	tracking_uri = os.environ.get("MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI")
108	if tracking_uri:
109	    mlflow.set_tracking_uri(tracking_uri)
110	if params.mlflow_experiment:
111	    mlflow.set_experiment(params.mlflow_experiment)
112	
113	run_ctx = mlflow.start_run(run_name=params.mlflow_run_name) if params.mlflow_experiment else None
114	
115	if run_ctx:
116	    mlflow.log_params({k: v for k, v in vars(params).items() if not k.startswith("mlflow_")})
117	
118	for epoch in range(params.epochs):
119	    avg_loss = train_one_epoch(...)
120	    if run_ctx:
121	        mlflow.log_metric("loss", avg_loss, step=epoch)
122	
123	if run_ctx:
124	    mlflow.end_run()
125	```
126	
127	Use `with mlflow.start_run(...) as run:` if you don't need conditional disable.
128	
129	## Live training widget (UI mode only)
130	
131	In edit mode, embed `mlflow_widgets.MlflowChart` so the user sees the loss curve update live as the training cell runs. Gate it off in script mode (no display surface):
132	
133	```python
134	from mlflow_widgets import MlflowChart
135	
136	if not is_script_mode and params.mlflow_experiment:
137	    chart = MlflowChart(
138	        tracking_uri=os.environ.get("MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI", "file:./mlruns"),
139	        experiment_name=params.mlflow_experiment,
140	        metric_key="loss",
141	    )
142	    widget = mo.ui.anywidget(chart)
143	    widget
144	```
145	
146	For comparing finished runs, swap `MlflowChart` → `MlflowRunTable` or `MlflowParallelCoordinates`. See [mlflow-widgets README](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/mlflow-widgets) for the full surface.
147	
148	## Environment Variables (EnvConfig)
149	
150	Keep upstream's `wigglystuff.EnvConfig` pattern but swap secrets:
151	
152	```python
153	from wigglystuff import EnvConfig
154	import mlflow
155	
156	env_config = mo.ui.anywidget(
157	    EnvConfig({
158	        "MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI": lambda u: mlflow.MlflowClient(tracking_uri=u).search_experiments(),
159	        "MLFLOW_TRACKING_TOKEN": lambda _: True,  # presence-only check
160	    })
161	)
162	env_config if not is_script_mode else None
163	```
164	
165	Place the `EnvConfig` cell near the top of the notebook, after imports, before the params form.
166	
167	## Columns
168	
169	Preserve upstream's column convention for navigability:
170	
171	```python
172	@app.cell(column=0, hide_code=True)
173	def _(mo):
174	    mo.md(r"""## Notebook Description""")
175	    return
176	```
177	
178	Recommended layout: `column=0` description + envs, `column=1` params form, `column=2` data setup, `column=3` model, `column=4` training loop + live chart.
179	
180	## Grid search
181	
182	For hyperparameter sweeps point users at [`references/grid.py`](references/grid.py). Same contract as upstream:
183	
184	- Dry run by default: `uv run grid.py` prints sampled combinations.
185	- `--launch` actually submits jobs.
186	- `--count N` and `--seed S` control sampling.
187	- Backend: Hugging Face Jobs via `huggingface_hub.run_uv_job`. Required secrets: `HF_TOKEN` and `MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI` (instead of upstream's `WANDB_API_KEY`).
188	
189	Swap HF Jobs for Modal / RunPod / local `subprocess.run([...])` by replacing the `run_uv_job` call — the rest of the script (search space, dedup, dry-run formatting) is provider-agnostic.
190	
191	## Workflow when the user invokes this skill
192	
193	1. Confirm the user wants the MLflow + Tyro variant (not upstream W&B + `mo.cli_args()`).
194	2. Ask which params they want exposed as CLI flags.
195	3. Ask: dataclass or Pydantic? Default to dataclass unless they need validators.
196	4. Ask: live `MlflowChart` cell yes/no? Default yes.
197	5. Verify proposed cell-level edits with the user before applying. Keep `@app.cell(column=N, hide_code=True)` markers intact.
198	6. If they want a sweep, copy `references/grid.py` next to their notebook and update the `SEARCH_SPACE` dict.
199

1	---
2	name: mlflow-tracking
3	description: Set up and operate MLflow for ML experiment tracking, model registry, and LLM tracing in any Python project. Covers three deployment modes — local file (`./mlruns`), local SQLite + `mlflow ui` (recommended for solo experiments), and a production Docker Compose stack with PostgreSQL + MinIO (vendored as a ready-to-copy `assets/docker-compose-stack/`). Use whenever the user wants to log params/metrics/artifacts, manage models with aliases (Champion/Challenger), enable framework autologging (sklearn/pytorch/lightning/xgboost/transformers/etc.), trace LLM calls (OpenAI/Anthropic/LangChain/LlamaIndex/DSPy), spin up a self-hosted tracking server, or asks about `mlflow.set_tracking_uri` / `mlflow.start_run` / `mlflow.<framework>.autolog` / `mlflow ui` / `MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI`. Always references the official docs at https://mlflow.org/docs/latest and the upstream repo https://github.com/mlflow/mlflow — MLflow ships fast, prefer fetching live docs over relying on memory.
4	---
5	
6	# MLflow Tracking
7	
8	MLflow gives you experiment tracking, a model registry, and (since 2.14+) first-class LLM observability — all from one Python library + UI. Unlike DVC it **does** require a tracking backend (file / SQLite / server), but it gives you a real dashboard and multi-user collaboration in return.
9	
10	This skill is opinionated about the **three deployment modes that actually get used in practice**, with a vendored production stack you can copy into any project. It defers to the official docs for everything else.
11	
12	## When to use
13	
14	- User wants to track ML experiments (params, metrics, artifacts) with a UI
15	- User mentions `mlflow.start_run`, `mlflow.log_metric`, `mlflow.set_tracking_uri`, `MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI`, `mlflow ui`
16	- User wants framework autologging (sklearn / PyTorch / Lightning / XGBoost / LightGBM / Keras / TensorFlow / Transformers / spark)
17	- User wants LLM trace observability (OpenAI, Anthropic, LangChain, LlamaIndex, DSPy, AutoGen, CrewAI, etc.)
18	- User wants to spin up a self-hosted tracking server with PostgreSQL + MinIO (production)
19	- User wants a model registry with aliases (Champion / Challenger / Production)
20	- User asks "how do I compare runs", "where do my logged params go", "how do I serve a logged model"
21	
22	## When NOT to use
23	
24	- User wants reproducible **pipelines** with data versioning → use `dvc-ml-workflow` skill
25	- User wants Weights & Biases specifically → MLflow is the open-source counterpart but not a drop-in replacement
26	- User wants DataBricks-managed MLflow → most code transfers, but auth/workspace setup is Databricks-specific; defer to Databricks docs
27	- User wants a single throwaway run with no UI → `print()` is fine; MLflow adds overhead
28	
29	## Authoritative sources (link these, don't paraphrase from memory)
30	
31	- Docs root: https://mlflow.org/docs/latest
32	- Tracking: https://mlflow.org/docs/latest/tracking.html
33	- Model Registry: https://mlflow.org/docs/latest/model-registry.html
34	- LLM tracing / GenAI: https://mlflow.org/docs/latest/llms/tracing/index.html
35	- Autologging matrix: https://mlflow.org/docs/latest/tracking/autolog.html
36	- Upstream repo: https://github.com/mlflow/mlflow
37	- PyPI: https://pypi.org/project/mlflow/
38	- mlflow-widgets (anywidget for live charts): https://github.com/daviddwlee84/mlflow-widgets
39	
40	MLflow ships a release roughly every 4–6 weeks. **Fetch the docs page** before answering version-specific questions (especially anything about LLM tracing, which is the fastest-moving area).
41	
42	## Decision: which deployment mode?
43	
44	Pick **before** writing any code. Switching later means migrating runs.
45	
46	| Mode | Tracking URI | When to choose | Read |
47	|---|---|---|---|
48	| **File** | `file:./mlruns` (default) | One-off experiments, no UI needed, no model registry | — |
49	| **SQLite + `mlflow ui`** ⭐ | `sqlite:///mlflow.db` | Solo work, small-to-medium experiment counts, want UI without running a server | `references/sqlite-local.md` |
50	| **Docker Compose stack** ⭐ | `http://host:8000` (PostgreSQL + MinIO) | Team use, production, parallel jobs, large artifacts, model registry across projects | `references/docker-compose-server.md` + `assets/docker-compose-stack/` |
51	| Databricks-managed | `databricks://` | Already paying for Databricks | (out of scope; defer to Databricks docs) |
52	
53	The two starred modes cover ~95% of real use. **Default**: SQLite for quick experiments, Docker Compose stack when more than one person needs to see the same runs.
54	
55	### File mode is for transient runs only
56	
57	The default `file:./mlruns` mode does NOT support the model registry — `mlflow.register_model()` raises. If the user wants a registry **at all**, they need SQLite or a server backend, even for solo use.
58	
59	## Workflow
60	
61	### 1. Initialize the chosen mode
62	
63	**SQLite (recommended for solo)**:
64	
65	```bash
66	bash skills/local/mlflow-tracking/scripts/init-mlflow-sqlite.sh
67	# Creates mlflow.db, .gitignore entries, prints the URL to launch `mlflow ui`
68	```
69	
70	**Docker Compose stack (recommended for team)**:
71	
72	```bash
73	bash skills/local/mlflow-tracking/scripts/start-mlflow-server.sh --target-dir infra/mlflow
74	# Copies assets/docker-compose-stack/ into infra/mlflow/, customizes .env,
75	# runs `docker compose up -d`, waits for the healthcheck, prints the URL.
76	```
77	
78	### 2. Set the tracking URI in your code
79	
80	```python
81	import mlflow
82	
83	# SQLite mode:
84	mlflow.set_tracking_uri("sqlite:///mlflow.db")
85	
86	# Server mode:
87	mlflow.set_tracking_uri("http://localhost:8000")
88	```
89	
90	Or via env var (preferred for subprocess / CI consistency):
91	
92	```bash
93	export MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI=sqlite:///mlflow.db
94	# or
95	export MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI=http://localhost:8000
96	```
97	
98	`set_tracking_uri()` only affects the current process. Subprocesses MUST use the env var.
99	
100	### 3. Log a run

# Bug Summary: Project-Level plansDirectory Setting Ignored

## Issue Overview
The `plansDirectory` setting in a project's `.claude/settings.json` is being **ignored** in favor of the global default path (`~/.claude/plans/`).

## Setting Scope
This is a **project-level setting** that should override the global default, but currently does not.

## Problem Details

**Steps to Reproduce:**
1. Create `.claude/settings.json` with:
```json
{
  "plansDirectory": ".claude/plans"
}
```
2. Create `.claude/plans/` directory in project root
3. Enter plan mode
4. Plan files are created in `~/.claude/plans/` (global path) instead of `./.claude/plans/` (project path)

## Expected vs Actual Behavior
- **Expected:** Plan files created in project-local `.claude/plans/` directory
- **Actual:** Files created in global `~/.claude/plans/` directory, ignoring the project setting

## Environment
- **Platform:** Linux
- **Severity:** Bug marked as confirmed with reproduction steps

## Status
**Closed** (Issue #19537 on anthropics/claude-code repository)

The issue indicates a configuration precedence problem where project-level settings should take priority over global defaults but currently don't.
```

# SpecStory CLI Overview

## Purpose
SpecStory CLI is a cross-platform command-line tool that captures AI coding conversations from terminal agents like Claude Code, Cursor CLI, and others. It converts these interactions into searchable markdown files and can sync them to SpecStory Cloud.

## Core Commands

**Run mode**: `specstory run <provider>` - Wraps agent execution with automatic markdown saving

**Sync mode**: `specstory sync <provider>` - Converts prior conversations to local markdown files

**Specific session**: `specstory sync -s <session-uuid>` - Processes individual sessions

## Output & Storage

**Local directory structure**: `.specstory/history/` (customizable via config)

**Filename format**: Sessions are saved as markdown files with sequential naming based on conversation metadata

**Active session detection**: The tool monitors agent data locations (e.g., `~/.claude/projects/` for Claude Code) to identify and process sessions

## Configuration

Settings use TOML format at two levels:
- User-level: `~/.specstory/cli/config.toml`
- Project-level: `.specstory/cli/config.toml`

CLI flags override both config file levels. Options control local/cloud sync behavior, logging, analytics, telemetry endpoints, and custom agent commands.

# Research — SpecStory, Claude Code plansDirectory, Gitleaks, Secret Remediation

Research for a Claude Code skill that helps agents commit SpecStory chat history and plan files alongside feature changes.

## 1. SpecStory

**What it is.** Local-first extension/CLI that captures AI coding conversations (Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, Codex, Gemini, Droid) and writes them as Markdown you can commit with your code. For Claude Code specifically, SpecStory reads raw session files from `~/.claude/projects/` (JSONL) and converts them to Markdown.

**On-disk layout.**
- Root: `.specstory/` inside each project.
- Conversations: `.specstory/history/*.md` — one Markdown file per session, timestamp-prefixed with session metadata in the header. Exact filename pattern is not documented verbatim, but docs uniformly describe them as "timestamped markdown files". You can assume a leading ISO-ish date for sorting.
- Derived rules backups (when that feature is on): `.specstory/ai_rules_backups/` — SpecStory auto-adds this subpath to `.gitignore`.

**CLI.** Installable via Homebrew (`brew tap specstoryai/tap && brew install specstory`). Relevant commands:
- `specstory check` — detect installed agents
- `specstory run claude` — launch Claude Code with autosave wrapping
- `specstory watch` — background capture for any supported agent
- `specstory list claude` — enumerate discoverable sessions
- `specstory sync claude` — convert prior sessions to Markdown in `.specstory/history/`
- `specstory sync claude -s <session-uuid>` — export one specific session

**Config.** TOML at two levels (CLI flags override both):
- User: `~/.specstory/cli/config.toml`
- Project: `.specstory/cli/config.toml`
- VS Code / Cursor extension also exposes `specstory.autoSave` (on by default).

**Identifying the active session.** There is no first-class "current session" selector. The practical approach:
1. `specstory list claude` lists sessions by UUID with timestamps.
2. Claude Code itself writes the live session JSONL under `~/.claude/projects/<slugified-cwd>/<session-uuid>.jsonl`. The most recently-modified JSONL in the slug matching the current repo is the active session; pass that UUID to `specstory sync claude -s <uuid>` to export exactly that conversation rather than everything.
3. Under `specstory run` / `specstory watch`, each invocation owns the file it produces, so "the file whose mtime is within the last few minutes" is the working heuristic a commit skill can use.

**`.gitignore` guidance.** Official integration doc explicitly says **commit `.specstory/history/` alongside your code to preserve design intent** — i.e. do **not** gitignore it. The tool only auto-ignores `.specstory/ai_rules_backups/`.

**Links.** [Docs features](https://docs.specstory.com/specstory/features) · [Claude Code integration](https://docs.specstory.com/integrations/claude-code) · [Quickstart](https://docs.specstory.com/quickstart) · [FAQs](https://docs.specstory.com/faqs) · [GitHub: specstoryai/getspecstory](https://github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory) · [CLI README](https://github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/blob/dev/specstory-cli/README.md).

## 2. Claude Code `plansDirectory`

**Confirmed setting.** `plansDirectory` is a valid key in `.claude/settings.json`. It controls where Plan Mode writes the generated plan Markdown file (the same kind of file this research is being written into right now). Default is the global `~/.claude/plans/` directory. Plan files are per-conversation markdown with slug-like names (e.g. `...skill-proud-sedgewick-agent-<hash>.md` as in the current session).

**Scope — user vs project.** Can be set in either:
- User-level `~/.claude/settings.json`, or
- Project-level `.claude/settings.json` (standard Claude Code precedence: local > project > user).

A user-level value means *every* project's plans land in the configured path (e.g. `~/Projects/AI-plans`) unless a project-level override exists. That answers the user's question: yes, you can globally force plans somewhere, but the *natural* way to get per-repo plan files committed with code is a project-level `"plansDirectory": ".claude/plans"` and adding that folder to the repo.

**Important caveat.** [anthropics/claude-code#19537](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/19537) reports the project-level `plansDirectory` being ignored in favor of `~/.claude/plans/` in some versions. The skill should verify by actually checking where the file landed after plan mode, not by trusting the setting alone.

**Links.** [ClaudeLog FAQ](https://claudelog.com/faqs/what-is-plans-directory-in-claude-code/) · [ghinda notes](https://notes.ghinda.com/post/claude-code-settings-default-to-plan-mode-and-plans-directory) · [Feature request #17473](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/17473) · [Bug #19537](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/19537).

## 3. Gitleaks for staged files

**Command.** `gitleaks protect --staged --redact` is the historical incantation. As of v8.19.0, `detect` and `protect` are deprecated in favor of the unified `gitleaks git` subcommand: `gitleaks git --staged --redact` (see [discussion #1811](https://github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks/discussions/1811)). A forward-compatible skill should prefer `gitleaks git --staged` and fall back to `gitleaks protect --staged` if the binary is older.

**Global hook wiring.** Two portable ways to enforce it without every project adopting pre-commit:
- `git config --global core.hooksPath ~/.config/git/hooks` + a `pre-commit` script there that runs `gitleaks git --staged --redact`. Applies to every repo this user clones.
- `git config --global init.templateDir ~/.git-template` with `hooks/pre-commit` inside it — only affects repos initialized *after* the config, so `core.hooksPath` is usually preferable for retrofitting.
- Either way, the hook should honor a `SKIP=gitleaks` env escape hatch and exit 0 if gitleaks isn't installed (don't brick commits on a fresh machine).

**Gotchas on SpecStory transcripts.**
- SpecStory history files are long and *contain verbatim agent output*, which routinely includes example tokens (`sk-...`, `ghp_...`, AWS-style AKIA fake keys used in docs). Gitleaks will fire on those. Mitigate with a project-scoped `.gitleaks.toml` allowlist:
  \```toml
  [allowlist]
  paths = [ '''\.specstory/history/.*\.md''' ]
  \```
  or a per-rule allowlist if you only want to suppress certain detectors on those paths. Allowlisting an entire transcript directory is pragmatic since real secrets should never have been typed into the chat in the first place; if they were, rotate them (see §4).
- Large files: `gitleaks git --staged` diff-scans the staged delta, so even a multi-MB transcript mostly costs O(diff) — but initial commits of a full history folder will scan the whole thing. Consider committing `.specstory/history/` incrementally.
- False positives on plan files are rarer but possible (LLM will echo example keys); apply the same allowlist approach to `.claude/plans/` if plan files are committed.

**Links.** [gitleaks repo](https://github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks) · [staged-only scanning discussion](https://github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks/discussions/1811) · [local pre-commit walkthrough (d4b.dev)](https://www.d4b.dev/blog/2026-02-01-gitleaks-pre-commit-hook/) · [IBM PTC Medium post](https://medium.com/@ibm_ptc_security/securing-your-repositories-with-gitleaks-and-pre-commit-27691eca478d).

## 4. "I already committed a secret" — canonical path

In priority order, and **without** reaching for force-push on shared history:

1. **Assume it's compromised. Rotate immediately.** Revoke/regenerate the token, key, or password at the provider. This is the only step that actually protects you. Everything else is hygiene.
2. **Stop the bleed on the working branch.** Remove the secret from the file(s), commit the fix, push. New clones of HEAD won't have it, even though history still does.
3. **Decide whether a history rewrite is worth it.** If the branch hasn't been pushed, or is a solo feature branch, use `git filter-repo --invert-paths --path <file>` (or BFG) and force-push with team coordination. On a shared/published branch the rewrite risks recontamination — any teammate's stale clone can `git pull` + `git push` the secret back. In practice: if you've rotated, leaving the old ciphertext in history is usually acceptable.
4. **GitHub-specific belt-and-braces:** ask GitHub Support to purge cached views/forks (the rewritten commit stays reachable via the SHA otherwise), and enable [push protection / secret scanning](https://docs.github.com/en/authentication/keeping-your-account-and-data-secure/removing-sensitive-data-from-a-repository) so the next one is caught before it lands.

Short version the skill should surface: **"Rotate first. Scrub second, only if cheap. Never rely on rewriting history to keep a secret secret."**

**Links.** [GitHub Docs: removing sensitive data](https://docs.github.com/en/authentication/keeping-your-account-and-data-secure/removing-sensitive-data-from-a-repository) · [Simon Willison TIL](https://til.simonwillison.net/git/rewrite-repo-remove-secrets) · [Microsoft Tech Community](https://techcommunity.microsoft.com/blog/azureinfrastructureblog/how-to-safely-remove-secrets-from-your-git-history-the-right-way/4464722).

## 3. Gitleaks
- **Staged scan:** `gitleaks protect --staged --redact` (deprecated since v8.19.0 → prefer `gitleaks git --staged --redact`).
- **Global hook:** `git config --global core.hooksPath ~/.config/git/hooks` with a `pre-commit` script calling gitleaks. Preferable to `init.templateDir` because it applies to already-cloned repos. Hook should support `SKIP=gitleaks` and soft-fail if the binary is absent.
- **SpecStory gotcha:** Transcripts echo example keys (`sk-...`, `ghp_...`, fake AKIA). Add a `.gitleaks.toml` allowlist for `.specstory/history/.*\.md` and `.claude/plans/.*\.md`. Performance-wise `--staged` only scans the diff, so normal commits are cheap; the first bulk commit of history is the expensive one.

## 4. Accidentally committed a secret
Canonical advice (avoids force-push reflex):
1. **Rotate immediately** at the provider — the only step that actually protects you.
2. **Remove from HEAD** and push a follow-up commit.
3. **Rewrite history only if cheap** (solo branch, not yet shared). Use `git filter-repo --invert-paths --path <file>` or BFG; on a shared branch this risks recontamination from stale teammate clones.
4. On GitHub, enable push protection / secret scanning and ask Support to purge cached views if needed.

Tagline for the skill: **"Rotate first. Scrub second, only if cheap. Never rely on rewriting history to keep a secret secret."**

# Design Doc: Agent-History Hygiene Skill

## 1. Skill name

**Recommendation: `agent-history-hygiene`** (picked).

Alternatives considered:
- `commit-agent-artifacts` — too verb-specific, misses the leak-prevention half.
- `specstory-plan-guardrails` — too tool-specific; will rot if SpecStory is replaced.

`agent-history-hygiene` wins because (a) "hygiene" cues both "commit the right things" *and* "don't leak secrets" under one roof, (b) it's tool-agnostic (SpecStory today, Cline/OpenCode/Cursor tomorrow), and (c) the word "history" maps cleanly to user trigger phrases like "commit my chat", "save this session", "specstory file".

## 2. SKILL.md outline

Frontmatter `description` (pushy, trigger-dense):

> Preserve agent chat transcripts (SpecStory `.specstory/history/*.md`), plan files (`.claude/plans/*.md`, `.cursor/plans/*.md`), and `.specify/` artifacts alongside the feature commit they belong to — without leaking `.env` contents or API keys into the git history. Use when the user says "commit my chat", "save this specstory session", "stage the plan file", "my agent session leaked a secret", "scrub the transcript", "bootstrap pre-commit for a new project", or when you notice untracked `.specstory/history/*.md` / `.claude/plans/*.md` files during a commit. Also use after a `git push` that exposed a key — to enforce rotate-first, rewrite-last remediation instead of reflexive `push --force`. Pairs with the chezmoi-installed `redact-agent-secrets` + `gitleaks` pre-commit hooks; this skill handles the invocation surface the hooks don't cover.

Section headings:

- **Core invariants** — three lines: (1) agent transcripts + plan files MUST be committed with the diff they produced, never `.gitignore`d; (2) secrets in a transcript are rotated at the provider *before* any git rewrite; (3) `--force` / history rewrites are a last resort and never against a shared branch.
- **When to use** — concrete phrases (see description); plus passive triggers ("you see a dirty `.specstory/history/` while running `git status`").
- **When NOT to use** — (a) the user explicitly wants transcripts excluded from the repo (offer one-liner `.gitignore` instead); (b) the leak is already on a shared branch with downstream clones — defer to `git-filter-repo` / BFG docs, don't try to unring it; (c) the project has no agent session at all.
- **Workflow A: commit-time hygiene** — identify session → stage artifacts alongside code → scan staged diff → commit.
- **Workflow B: bootstrap a new project** — copy `.pre-commit-config.yaml` + `.gitleaks.toml` templates → `pre-commit install` → sanity-check `.gitignore` doesn't silently hide `.claude/plans/`.
- **Workflow C: post-leak remediation** — rotate-at-provider checklist → assess branch-shared-ness → redact in place + new commit (preferred) → only if unshared + unpushed, `git commit --amend` / `git filter-repo`.
- **Gotchas** — six items:
  1. `plansDirectory` in `~/.claude/settings.json` is `./.claude/plans` per-project, not a global path.
  2. SpecStory CLI vs VS Code extension write to the same dir but with different session-UUID conventions.
  3. `gitleaks protect --staged` is deprecated ≥ v8.19.0 → use `gitleaks git --staged --redact`.
  4. `pre-commit install` is per-clone, so CI and teammates must also install or enforce via hook.
  5. `.specstory/history/` files can be huge; a single "commit everything" sweep can balloon diffs. Scope by mtime/session.
  6. chezmoi's global `core.hooksPath` means repo-level hooks never run unless `.pre-commit-config.yaml` or gitleaks is present — don't expect a bare repo to be protected.
- **Integration with chezmoi infrastructure** — short section pointing at the user's existing `redact-agent-secrets` hook and `.gitleaks.toml`; clarifies what the skill adds (the invocation wrapper) vs what chezmoi owns (the rules).
- **Available scripts** and **Reference files** — standard sections.

Target ~350 lines; anything longer moves to `references/`.

## 3. Scripts to ship (4)

**`scripts/find-session.sh`** — resolve the current agent session for `$PWD`.
- CLI: `find-session.sh [--json] [--format=specstory|claude|both]`
- Output (stdout, TSV by default):
  ```
  specstory_path<TAB>/abs/path/.specstory/history/2026-04-24_10-30-abc.md
  claude_session_uuid<TAB>1f3e…
  claude_jsonl_path<TAB>/Users/…/.claude/projects/<slug>/1f3e….jsonl
  ```
- Implementation: Claude UUID = newest `*.jsonl` in `~/.claude/projects/<cwd-slug>/` (slug = `$PWD` with `/` → `-`). SpecStory path = newest `*.md` in `$PWD/.specstory/history/`. Fall back gracefully (print empty TSV rows with stderr diagnostic), never fail the agent's pipeline.

**`scripts/stage-agent-artifacts.sh`** — `git add` the right files before commit.
- CLI: `stage-agent-artifacts.sh [--dry-run] [--include-all-plans] [--session-only]`
- Default behavior: stages (a) the current SpecStory file from `find-session.sh`, (b) all unstaged `.claude/plans/*.md`, (c) `.cursor/plans/*.md`, `.opencode/plans/*.md`, `.specify/**` if present. `--session-only` suppresses (b–d). `--include-all-plans` also grabs historical plan files that git already tracks but were modified.
- Refuses to run if HEAD is clean of code changes and no artifacts are dirty (avoids the "commit just the transcript" anti-pattern → should be paired with a diff).

**`scripts/bootstrap-project.sh`** — scaffold hooks into a new repo.
- CLI: `bootstrap-project.sh [--from-chezmoi] [--force] [--dry-run]`
- Actions: (a) copy `assets/pre-commit-config.yaml.template` → `.pre-commit-config.yaml` if absent; (b) copy `assets/gitleaks.toml.template` → `.gitleaks.toml` if absent; (c) `uvx pre-commit@4 install` (pinned); (d) audit `.gitignore` — warn (don't edit) if `.claude/plans/` or `.specstory/` matches an ignore pattern; (e) audit `.git/info/exclude` similarly.
- `--from-chezmoi`: symlinks to `~/.local/share/chezmoi/.pre-commit-config.yaml` / `.gitleaks.toml` instead of copying, so updates propagate. Mention tradeoff in help.

**`scripts/scan-staged.sh`** — run `gitleaks` on the staged diff with agent-friendly exit codes.
- CLI: `scan-staged.sh [--redact] [--no-redact] [--verbose]`
- Uses `gitleaks git --staged --redact` (not deprecated `protect`). Exit codes: 0 = clean; 10 = leaks found + redact applied; 20 = leaks found + `--no-redact`; 30 = gitleaks not installed (print install hint).
- Structured stdout: JSON lines of findings (rule, file, line). Prose to stderr.

That's 4 scripts. I considered a fifth `remediate-leak.sh` but remediation is too branchy to automate safely — it stays as a `references/remediation.md` checklist.

## 4. Reference files (3)

- **`references/transcript-session-discovery.md`** — deep dive on SpecStory's session-UUID conventions (CLI `specstory sync claude -s <uuid>` vs extension autosave), the `~/.claude/projects/<slug>/*.jsonl` Claude Code internal format, and the `$PWD` → slug algorithm. Load when `find-session.sh` returns empty or ambiguous results.
- **`references/pre-commit-redaction-stack.md`** — explains the layered defense: chezmoi's `redact-agent-secrets` → `gitleaks-system` → skill's `scan-staged.sh` as belt-and-suspenders. Documents how `.gitleaksignore` and inline `# gitleaks:allow` pragmas work for in-transcript example keys. Load when the user hits an unexpected block or wants to tune rules.
- **`references/remediation.md`** — the post-leak runbook. Rotate-first tree: (1) identify provider → rotate in-console URLs; (2) confirm blast radius (is it pushed? which branches?); (3) if unshared local → amend or `git reset --soft HEAD~ && redact && recommit`; (4) if shared → `git-filter-repo` + force-with-lease on feature branches only; (5) audit downstream clones. Load after `scan-staged.sh` finds a real leak or the user says "I already pushed".

## 5. Assets (templates, not symlinks)

**Decision: ship *copies* of the chezmoi templates under `assets/`**, not references.

Tradeoff: symlinks / "read from chezmoi" would keep templates DRY but (a) breaks for users who install this skill without chezmoi, (b) couples skill versioning to the user's machine state, (c) `npx skills@latest add` can't resolve a path that doesn't exist on the target. Copies are the right default; `bootstrap-project.sh --from-chezmoi` is the escape hatch for users who *do* run chezmoi and want live updates.

Assets:

- `assets/pre-commit-config.yaml.template` — minimal `.pre-commit-config.yaml` with the `redact-agent-secrets` local hook + `gitleaks` hook, using `gitleaks git --staged --redact`. Includes placeholder `{{REDACT_SCRIPT_PATH}}` — bootstrap resolves to either `~/.local/share/chezmoi/scripts/redact_secrets.py` (if chezmoi present) or a bundled copy.
- `assets/gitleaks.toml.template` — subset of the user's chezmoi `.gitleaks.toml`: the custom rules for OpenAI/Anthropic/WakaTime/Cursor/HuggingFace/Supabase/Linear/Tailscale/Notion, plus a new `[[allowlist]]` block for `.specstory/history/**` that whitelists fenced code blocks tagged as `example` or `redacted` so in-transcript demo keys don't trip detection.
- `assets/redact_secrets.py` — bundled copy of the chezmoi script (PEP 723 header, `--fix`, `--check`) so the skill is self-contained for non-chezmoi users. Document drift risk in `references/pre-commit-redaction-stack.md` (single source of truth: chezmoi; skill copy is the fallback).
- `assets/gitignore-audit.txt` — one-line list of patterns the bootstrap audit flags (`.claude/`, `.specstory/`, `.claude/plans/`, etc.) so the rule set is editable without touching bash.

## 6. Chezmoi changes (minimal)

Three small additions to `/Users/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi/`:

1. **`.gitleaks.toml` allowlist for SpecStory/plan transcripts.** Add:
   ```toml
   [[allowlists]]
   description = "In-transcript example keys in agent history files"
   paths = ['''\.specstory/history/.*\.md$''', '''\.claude/plans/.*\.md$''', '''\.cursor/plans/.*\.md$''']
   regexTarget = "line"
   regexes = ['''example[-_]?(key|token|secret)''', '''REDACTED''', '''sk-[a-zA-Z0-9]{3,8}\.\.\.''']
   ```
   Rationale: agents legitimately discuss key *shapes* in plans; the allowlist is narrow (paths × pattern both required).

2. **One-shot chezmoi script `run_once_before_install_hooks.sh.tmpl`** → *skip this*. A per-repo bootstrap is better handled by `bootstrap-project.sh` invoked on demand. A chezmoi `run_once_` fires globally, which is wrong for per-repo installs. Don't add.

3. **Update `redact_secrets.py`** — if the allowlist patterns above need to be consistent, add the same "example-key shape" exemption to the redactor so pre-commit doesn't redact legitimate documentation. One-line change; document in the skill's references.

4. **Flip `gitleaks protect --staged` → `gitleaks git --staged --redact`** in `dot_config/git/hooks/executable_pre-commit.tmpl`. It's deprecated; low-risk swap.

That's it. The user's infrastructure is already 90% there; the skill is the glue.

## 7. Registration

## 8. Verification plan

End-to-end test using a throwaway repo (read-only for the skill design; do at implementation time):

1. `mktemp -d && cd $_ && git init && echo hi > README.md && git add . && git commit -m init`
2. Run `bootstrap-project.sh` → confirm `.pre-commit-config.yaml`, `.gitleaks.toml` present, `pre-commit install` hook installed in `.git/hooks/pre-commit`, no gitignore-audit warnings.
3. Fake a plan file: `mkdir -p .claude/plans && printf '# plan\nuse OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-proj-realish-looking-fake' > .claude/plans/p1.md`.
4. Fake a SpecStory transcript with similar content at `.specstory/history/2026-04-24_test.md`.
5. `stage-agent-artifacts.sh --dry-run` → expect both files listed.
6. Edit code: `echo 'change' >> README.md`; `git add README.md`; `stage-agent-artifacts.sh` (for real); `scan-staged.sh` → expect exit 10, redacted in place.
7. `git diff --staged` → confirm the `sk-proj-…` value is replaced by `REDACTED`, but surrounding prose intact.
8. `git commit -m "feat"` → expect pre-commit to pass (already redacted by script).
9. Negative test: insert a real-shape key (`sk-ant-api03-` + 95 chars), no code change → `scan-staged.sh` still catches it → `git commit` → pre-commit blocks.
10. Simulate `.env` echo: `echo 'OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-proj-…' >> .claude/plans/p1.md`; re-run the redactor; confirm fix.
11. Remediation drill: `git reset --soft HEAD~1` after a "bad" commit, redact, recommit; compare with `git reflog` that no force-push was needed.

## 9. Open questions

1. **Bundled `redact_secrets.py` — copy or dynamic fetch?** I recommended bundling (self-contained). Confirm this vs a `--from-chezmoi` symlink default. Trade: staleness vs self-sufficiency.
2. **Should `stage-agent-artifacts.sh` be wired as a git hook, or stay agent-invoked?** A `prepare-commit-msg` hook would auto-stage on every commit (zero agent reliance) but may surprise users who `git commit` small interactive edits. I lean agent-invoked + documented; confirm.
3. **Scope of "session discovery" — SpecStory only, or include `.specify/` (GitHub spec-kit) and `.cursor/` history too?** Including everything makes the skill broader but risks false positives in repos with stale `.cursor/` dirs. I lean: SpecStory + Claude plans by default; other dirs opt-in via flag. Confirm.

**SpecStory behaviors**:
- Writes `.specstory/history/<timestamp>.md` per session. Official docs say commit these with code, don't .gitignore.
- No first-class "which session is mine" selector. Heuristic: find newest `.jsonl` in `~/.claude/projects/<cwd-slug>/` to get the active session UUID, then call `specstory sync claude -s <uuid>`, OR just take the most recently modified file in `.specstory/history/`.
- `specstory.autoSave` via VS Code extension writes continuously; CLI `specstory run claude` wraps the CLI.

**The problem this skill solves**:
1. LLMs (by default) treat `.specstory/history/**.md` and `.claude/plans/**.md` as "generated artifacts" and exclude them from commits. User wants the OPPOSITE default: these MUST be staged alongside the feature diff.
2. Agents sometimes echo env vars / `.env` contents into chat → secrets land in transcripts → committed. Need a "before push" safety net even though pre-commit redact-agent-secrets already exists.
3. New projects that don't have `.pre-commit-config.yaml` installed yet: skill should scaffold one quickly without per-repo drudgery.
4. After an accidental secret leak: avoid the "force-push to scrub history" reflex. Rotate at the provider first; only rewrite history if the branch is unshared.

```text
1	---
2	name: skill-author
3	description: Author a new agent skill or refactor an existing one to follow agentskills.io best practices — gotchas sections, output templates, validation loops, calibrated specificity (fragility-based), and agentic script design (--help, --dry-run, structured stdout, stderr diagnostics, PEP 723 inline deps, pinned uvx/npx versions). Use whenever the user wants to create a new skill from scratch, scaffold a SKILL.md, write a reference file, design a script meant to be invoked by an agent, lint a draft skill for quality, or convert an ad-hoc workflow into a reusable skill. For evaluating skill output quality with test cases, benchmarking, or optimizing the description trigger rate, defer to the `skill-creator` skill instead — this skill focuses on authoring, not evaluation.
4	---
5	
6	# Skill Author
7	
8	Helps you write **new agent skills** that follow the best-practices documented at
9	https://agentskills.io/skill-creation/ — without you having to re-read those pages
10	every time. Pairs with `skill-creator` (which handles eval/iterate/optimize loops
11	once a draft exists).
12	
13	## When to use this vs `skill-creator`
14	
15	| Task | Use |
16	|---|---|
17	| "I want to make a new skill for X" | **skill-author** (scaffold + author) |
18	| "Scaffold the SKILL.md / a reference / a script" | **skill-author** |
19	| "Lint this skill draft" | **skill-author** |
20	| "My skill isn't triggering when I want it to" | `skill-creator` (description optimization) |
21	| "Run test cases against my skill, benchmark it" | `skill-creator` (eval loop) |
22	| "Compare two versions of my skill" | `skill-creator` (blind comparison) |
23	
24	If both apply, start here, then hand off to `skill-creator` once the draft is solid.
25	
26	## Workflow
27	
28	### 1. Capture intent (1 minute)
29	
30	Before scaffolding, get four answers — usually just by asking the user:
31	
32	1. **What does it do?** (one sentence)
33	2. **When should it trigger?** (specific user phrases / contexts)
34	3. **What does it output?** (file, command result, plan, prose)
35	4. **Is the output objectively verifiable?** (decides whether `skill-creator` evals are worth the effort later)
36	
37	Write these four down before touching files. They become the seeds for the
38	description, the workflow body, and the future eval set.
39	
40	### 2. Scaffold
41	
42	Use `scripts/new-skill.sh` to produce the directory layout:
43	
44	```bash
45	bash skills/local/skill-author/scripts/new-skill.sh <skill-name>
46	# creates: skills/local/<skill-name>/{SKILL.md,references/,scripts/,assets/}
47	# seeds:   SKILL.md from assets/SKILL.md.template
48	```
49	
50	The template's frontmatter has placeholders that lint will reject — this is on
51	purpose so the agent can't forget to fill them in.
52	
53	### 3. Author the SKILL.md
54	
55	Read `references/authoring-patterns.md` before writing the body. The patterns
56	that matter most:
57	
58	- **Description must be "pushy"** and include concrete trigger contexts. Naive
59	  descriptions cause undertriggering — the #1 failure mode of new skills.
60	- **Gotchas section** — environment-specific facts that defy reasonable
61	  assumptions. The single highest-value section in most skills.
62	- **Output templates** — agents pattern-match against concrete structures more
63	  reliably than they follow prose descriptions of formats.
64	- **Calibrated specificity** — be prescriptive only where the task is fragile;
65	  give the agent freedom (and explain *why*) where multiple approaches are valid.
66	- **Defaults, not menus** — pick one tool/approach and mention alternatives as
67	  escape hatches.
68	
69	Keep `SKILL.md` under 500 lines. If you blow past that, move detail into
70	`references/<topic>.md` and tell the agent **when** to load it ("Read X if Y
71	happens"), not just that it exists.
72	
73	### 4. Design any scripts
74	
75	Before writing a script, read `references/script-design.md`. Skills script
76	design is meaningfully different from "regular" CLI script design because the
77	caller is an LLM reading your stderr to decide what to do next. The non-obvious
78	requirements:
79	
80	- No interactive prompts, ever (agents run in non-interactive shells)
81	- `--help` is the primary interface documentation — keep it concise but complete
82	- Errors must say *what was expected* and *what to try*, not just *what failed*
83	- Structured stdout (JSON/CSV/TSV), prose diagnostics to stderr — separate them
84	- `--dry-run` for any destructive operation
85	- Pin versions for `uvx` / `npx` / `pipx` invocations
86	
87	For Python helpers, prefer **PEP 723 inline dependencies** + `uv run` over
88	`requirements.txt` — the script becomes self-contained and the agent doesn't
89	have to set up an environment first.
90	
91	### 5. Lint
92	
93	Run the linter before committing or handing off to `skill-creator`:
94	
95	```bash
96	bash skills/local/skill-author/scripts/lint-skill.sh skills/local/<skill-name>
97	```
98	
99	It checks three things:
100	
101	1. **Frontmatter & length** — `name` and `description` exist; description has a
102	   "use when" trigger phrase; SKILL.md is under 500 lines.
103	2. **Script hygiene** — every `scripts/*.sh` has a shebang, is executable, and
104	   responds to `--help` (presence of the flag handler, not necessarily a working
105	   script).
106	3. **Reference reachability** — every file in `references/` is mentioned at
107	   least once from `SKILL.md` (no dead reference docs).
108	
109	Fix every error. Warnings are advisory but usually worth addressing.
110	
111	### 6. (Optional) Hand off to skill-creator
112	
113	Once lint passes and the skill *looks* right, the next questions are
114	quantitative: does it trigger reliably? does it produce good output? That's
115	`skill-creator` territory. Tell the user: "skill-author got the structure
116	right. If you want to validate it works on real prompts, the `skill-creator`
117	skill runs test cases and benchmarks."
118	
119	## Available scripts
120	
121	- **`scripts/new-skill.sh <name>`** — Scaffold `skills/local/<name>/` with
122	  SKILL.md, references/, scripts/, assets/ from templates.
123	  - Flags: `--vendor` (use `skills/vendor/<name>/` instead — rare, normally
124	    vendored skills come via `vendor.yaml`); `--dry-run`; `--force` (overwrite
125	    existing).
126	- **`scripts/lint-skill.sh <skill-dir>`** — Run frontmatter, script hygiene,
127	  and reference reachability checks. Exit non-zero on any error.
128	  - Flags: `--strict` (treat warnings as errors); `--quiet` (only print failures).
129	
130	## Bundled assets
131	
132	Templates that `new-skill.sh` copies and that you can reference manually:
133	
134	- `assets/SKILL.md.template` — Frontmatter + workflow skeleton with placeholders.
135	- `assets/reference.md.template` — Reference doc skeleton (TOC + sections).
136	- `assets/script-bash.template` — Bash 3.2 compatible script with `set -euo pipefail`,
137	  `--help` / `--dry-run` flag handler, structured-output friendly logging
138	  (data → stdout, prose → stderr).
139	- `assets/script-python.template` — Python script with PEP 723 inline-deps
140	  block, argparse with help/examples, dry-run support.
141	
142	## Reference files
143	
144	- `references/authoring-patterns.md` — The agentskills.io "best practices"
145	  page condensed: gotchas, templates, validation loops, calibrated specificity,
146	  defaults-not-menus, procedures-over-declarations, plan-validate-execute.
147	- `references/script-design.md` — The agentskills.io "using scripts" page
148	  condensed: agentic CLI design, structured output, error message style,
149	  PEP 723, uvx/npx/pipx version pinning, dry-run patterns.
150	- `references/this-repo-conventions.md` — Conventions specific to *this*
151	  repository: where to put local vs vendor skills, how the 5-level skill
152	  search works, AGENTS.md ↔ CLAUDE.md sync, where mirrored scripts live.
153	
154	## Gotchas
155	
156	- **AGENTS.md is a symlink to CLAUDE.md** — edit either one; never replace the
157	  symlink with a real file.
158	- **Skill discovery is one level deep first, then recursive up to 5 levels.**
159	  `skills/local/<name>/SKILL.md` works because of the recursive fallback. Don't
160	  nest skills more than 5 deep or they become invisible.
161	- **`bash 3.2` compatibility** is required for any script that might run on
162	  stock macOS. No `mapfile`, no `${var,,}` lowercasing, no `[[ -v var ]]`.
163	  See `references/script-design.md` for the safe subset.
164	- **`description` field length matters less than its trigger surface area.**
165	  A 200-word description that names 8 concrete contexts will outperform a
166	  50-word one that's beautifully concise but vague. Err on the side of more
167	  trigger phrases.
168	- **Don't write a skill that wraps something the agent already does well.**
169	  If a stock Claude session handles the task in one turn without help, a skill
170	  adds context-window cost for no gain. Test the no-skill baseline before
171	  investing in authoring.
172	
173	## When the user is updating an existing skill (not creating new)
174	
175	Same workflow, but skip step 2 (scaffold). Read the existing SKILL.md first,
176	identify which patterns from `references/authoring-patterns.md` are missing or
177	weakly applied, and propose edits one section at a time so the user can sanity
178	check. After edits, run lint, then offer the `skill-creator` handoff for
179	quantitative validation.
180
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
1	---
2	name: project-knowledge-harness
3	description: Set up a structured project memory for any software project — TODO.md as priority/effort-tagged index of future work, backlog/ for resume-friendly research/design notes on P? items, and pitfalls/ as a symptom-grep-able knowledge base of past traps. Use when a user wants somewhere to record "maybe later" ideas, freeze troubleshooting state, capture trade-off analysis, or stop re-debugging the same problem.
4	---
5	
6	# project-knowledge-harness
7	
8	A lightweight, file-based memory harness for any software project.
9	
10	Three surfaces, sharply separated by **time direction** and **access pattern**:
11	
12	| Surface | Time | Question it answers | Access pattern |
13	|---|---|---|---|
14	| `TODO.md` | Future | "What might we do later?" | Read top to bottom (priority lanes) |
15	| `backlog/<slug>.md` | Future | "What was the analysis behind this idea?" | Indexed from `TODO.md` |
16	| `pitfalls/<slug>.md` | **Past** | **"I see error X — has this happened before?"** | **Grep symptom keywords** |
17	
18	Plus, in projects that already have agent contracts, `AGENTS.md` Hard
19	invariants answer "What rules MUST agents follow?". Pitfalls *graduate* to
20	Hard invariants when serious enough — see
21	[`references/when-to-add-docs.md`](references/when-to-add-docs.md).
22	
23	## When to use this skill
24	
25	Use this skill when the user surfaces any of:
26	
27	- A long-term TODO list with no home, or a messy `TODO.md` that needs
28	  structure (signals: "where should ideas go?", "maybe later", "工程量太大需要再評估")
29	- A debugging session worth saving (signals: "keep solving the same problem
30	  twice", "save this troubleshooting", "踩過的坑", "TROUBLESHOOTING.md
31	  scattered across docs/")
32	- A request to consolidate `IDEAS.md` / `ROADMAP.md` / `WISHLIST.md` /
33	  `LESSONS.md` files
34	
35	Do NOT use this skill for active sprint planning (use issue trackers),
36	ephemeral agent scratchpads (use `.claude/plans/`), or current feature
37	documentation (use `docs/`).
38	
39	## How to apply this skill (default workflow)
40	
41	The skill bundles five scripts and several templates. **Default to the
42	init script** for setup, and **default to `add-todo.sh` / `sweep-inbox.sh`
43	for capture** rather than asking the agent to edit `TODO.md` by hand.
44	
45	```
46	scripts/
47	  init.sh         # one-shot setup of TODO.md + backlog/ + pitfalls/
48	                  # + agent guidance + README snippet
49	  todo-kanban.sh  # validate TODO.md format and render kanban-style board
50	  add-todo.sh     # insert a structured entry into the right ## P* lane
51	  promote-todo.sh # move an active TODO item to ## Done with the right syntax
52	  sweep-inbox.sh  # triage backlog/inbox.md into TODO.md via add-todo.sh
53	```
54	
55	### 1. Run `scripts/init.sh` against the target repo
56	
57	```sh
58	scripts/init.sh \
59	  --target /path/to/project \
60	  --project-name "My Project" \
61	  --deployment chezmoi   # or npm | pip | docker | none
62	```
63	
64	The script:
65	
66	1. Creates `TODO.md`, `backlog/README.md`, `pitfalls/README.md` from
67	   `assets/*.template`, substituting placeholders.
68	2. Appends an agent-guidance snippet to `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md` (auto-detected,
69	   override with `--agent-contract`).
70	3. Appends a "Roadmap & lessons learned" section to `README.md`.
71	4. Runs `scripts/todo-kanban.sh --validate-only TODO.md` so any drift is
72	   caught immediately.
73	5. Prints the deployment-exclusion lines you should add manually (it does
74	   not edit ignore files — see
75	   [`references/deployment-exclusion.md`](references/deployment-exclusion.md)).
76	
77	`init.sh` is idempotent: existing files are skipped unless `--force` is
78	given, and snippets append only if a sentinel marker is missing.
79	
80	### 2. Mid-conversation, when the user surfaces a "maybe later" idea
81	
82	Signals: "maybe later", "nice to have", "if I'm interested",
83	"工程量太大需要再評估", "先記下來", "not now but…".
84	
85	1. If `TODO.md` doesn't exist yet, run `scripts/init.sh` first.
86	2. **Default path — call `scripts/add-todo.sh`** with the priority,
87	   effort, title, and description. This inserts the canonical line into
88	   the right `## P*` lane and re-validates. Add `--backlog` if the
89	   conversation produced enough investigation that a `backlog/<slug>.md`
90	   doc is worth scaffolding.
91	
92	   ```sh
93	   scripts/add-todo.sh --priority "P?" --effort M \
94	     --title "Try Rspress for docs" \
95	     --description "Evaluate AI-native docs framework alternative"
96	   ```
97	
98	3. **Quick-capture path — append to `backlog/inbox.md`** when the user
99	   isn't sure of priority/effort yet, or is mid-thought:
100	
101	   ```sh
102	   echo "- $UNSTRUCTURED_THOUGHT" >> backlog/inbox.md
103	   ```
104	
105	   Later (this session or next), run `scripts/sweep-inbox.sh` to
106	   formalize the loose lines into `TODO.md` one at a time. The sweeper
107	   prompts for missing fields per line; in `--batch` mode it only
108	   processes lines that already have `priority=… effort=… title="…"
109	   description="…"` pairs and leaves ambiguous ones in place.
110	
111	4. **Manual edit path — only when scripts can't help.** Use the syntax
112	   from [`references/tag-schema.md`](references/tag-schema.md) and run
113	   `scripts/todo-kanban.sh --validate-only` afterwards.
114	
115	5. If you wrote a `backlog/<slug>.md` (either via `--backlog` or by
116	   hand), make sure the TODO line ends with
117	   ` → [research](backlog/<slug>.md)` so the index points to the doc.
118	
119	### 3. Mid-conversation, when you finish debugging something tricky
120	
121	Signals: "phew, that took a while", "weird, the error didn't say anything
122	about X", "this is the third time we've hit this", or you find yourself
123	reconstructing context that isn't in any doc.
124	
125	1. Create `pitfalls/<symptom-slug>.md` immediately from
126	   `assets/pitfall-doc.md.template`, while the trace is fresh. Title the
127	   doc by the **symptom**, not the root cause — you'll search by what
128	   you're seeing, not by what you eventually learned.
129	2. Copy verbatim error messages — never paraphrase, it kills grep-ability.
130	3. If the trap is severe (silent corruption / cross-machine recurrence /
131	   non-obvious workaround), surface it: "should this graduate to a Hard
132	   invariant in AGENTS.md?" — see
133	   [`references/when-to-add-docs.md`](references/when-to-add-docs.md).
134	
135	### 4. When implementing a `TODO.md` item
136	
137	In the same commit:
138	
139	1. Run `scripts/promote-todo.sh --title "<substring>" --summary "<what shipped>"`.
140	   It removes the active line and inserts the dated `Done` entry, then
141	   re-validates. It refuses to run if the substring matches zero or more
142	   than one active item.
143	2. If a `backlog/<slug>.md` exists, set its `Status: shipped` (don't
144	   delete — historical record may inform adjacent decisions).
145	3. If shipping uncovered a trap, write a `pitfalls/<slug>.md` for it.
146	
147	## When a TODO entry needs a `backlog/` doc, when a debug needs a `pitfalls/` doc
148	
149	Decision rules and the upgrade path to `AGENTS.md` invariants live in
150	[`references/when-to-add-docs.md`](references/when-to-add-docs.md). Read it
151	the first time you set up the harness; consult it again whenever you're
152	unsure which surface a piece of knowledge belongs in.
153	
154	## Tag schema
155	
156	Two orthogonal axes, validated by `scripts/todo-kanban.sh`. See
157	[`references/tag-schema.md`](references/tag-schema.md) for the full schema,
158	useful tag combinations, and the exact validator-checked syntax.
159	
160	## Anti-patterns
161	
162	Common mistakes to avoid (e.g., spawning `IDEAS.md` alongside `TODO.md`,
163	titling pitfalls by root cause, paraphrasing errors). Full list in
164	[`references/anti-patterns.md`](references/anti-patterns.md).
165	
166	## Deployment exclusion
167	
168	`TODO.md`, `backlog/`, and `pitfalls/` are maintainer-facing repo metadata,
169	not files to ship. Cheatsheet for chezmoi / npm / pip / Docker in
170	[`references/deployment-exclusion.md`](references/deployment-exclusion.md).
171	`scripts/init.sh --deployment ...` prints the exact lines to add.
172	
173	## Templates and bundled assets
174	
175	- `assets/TODO.md.template` — `TODO.md` skeleton with example items per lane
176	- `assets/backlog-README.md.template` — `backlog/` index + when-to-add rules
177	- `assets/backlog-doc.md.template` — single backlog doc (context-first)
178	- `assets/pitfalls-README.md.template` — `pitfalls/` index + cross-reference
179	  table for traps documented elsewhere
180	- `assets/pitfall-doc.md.template` — single pitfall doc (symptom-first)
181	- `assets/agent-guidance.md.template` — snippet for `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md`
182	- `assets/readme-roadmap.md.template` — snippet for project `README.md`
183	- `scripts/init.sh` — one-shot setup
184	- `scripts/todo-kanban.sh` — validator + Markdown kanban renderer
185	  (also supports `--json` and `--validate-only`)
186	- `scripts/add-todo.sh` — structured insert into `## P*` lane;
187	  `--backlog` also scaffolds `backlog/<slug>.md`
188	- `scripts/promote-todo.sh` — atomic active-→-Done move with re-validation
189	- `scripts/sweep-inbox.sh` — triage `backlog/inbox.md` → `add-todo.sh`
190	
191	## Reference implementation
192	
193	A live example of this harness is at
194	[`daviddwlee84/dotfiles`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles):
195	
196	- `TODO.md`, `backlog/`, `pitfalls/` directories at repo root
197	- `AGENTS.md` `### Long-term backlog → TODO.md + backlog/` and
198	  `### Past pitfalls → pitfalls/` sections
199	- `README.md` `## Roadmap & lessons learned` section
200

1	# Agent Skills
2	
3	A personal collection of [agent skills](https://agentskills.io/home) — both custom-authored and cherry-picked from upstream repos — installable as a single package.
4	
5	📚 **[Read the docs](https://daviddwlee84.github.io/agent-skills/)** for the full guide, conventions, and skill index.
6	
7	## Install
8	
9	<!-- snippet:install (keep in sync with docs/_snippets/install.md) -->
10	```bash
11	npx skills@latest add daviddwlee84/agent-skills/skills
12	```
13	
14	> **Note**
15	> The trailing `/skills` matters. Without it, `npx skills` will look in
16	> `.agents/skills/` of the upstream repo, which contains a different
17	> layout. The `skills/` suffix points the installer at the
18	> `skills/local/` and `skills/vendor/` trees.
19	<!-- /snippet:install -->
20	
21	## What's in here
22	
23	- **`skills/local/`** — custom-authored skills.

48	## Repo memory
49	
50	This repo dogfoods `project-knowledge-harness` on itself:
51	
52	- [`TODO.md`](TODO.md) — priority/effort-tagged backlog.
53	- [`backlog/`](backlog/) — research notes for `P?` items (when populated).
54	- [`backlog/inbox.md`](backlog/) — quick-capture inbox; sweep into `TODO.md` later.
55	- [`pitfalls/`](pitfalls/) — symptom-grep-able knowledge base of past traps (when populated).
56	
57	```bash
58	# Validate TODO.md and render kanban-style board
59	make kanban
60	
61	# Quick add structured TODO entry
62	./scripts/add-todo.sh --priority P3 --effort M --title "..." --description "..."
63	
64	# Move an active TODO to ## Done in same commit as the implementation
65	./scripts/promote-todo.sh --title "<substring>" --summary "<shipped summary>"
66	
67	# Triage backlog/inbox.md interactively
68	./scripts/sweep-inbox.sh
69	```
70	
71	Full workflow: [Project memory](https://daviddwlee84.github.io/agent-skills/workflows/project-memory/).
72	
73	## Vendor system
74	
75	```bash
76	# Add a vendored skill (auto-syncs)
77	./scripts/add-vendor.sh owner/repo/path/to/skill
78	# or via Makefile
79	make add-vendor SOURCE=owner/repo/path/to/skill
80	
81	# Group into a series subdir (skills/vendor/<series>/<name>/)
82	./scripts/add-vendor.sh --series fullstack-nextjs vercel/vercel-plugin/skills/nextjs
83	
84	# Sync all vendored skills from upstream
85	make sync
86	
87	# Check for upstream updates (dry-run)
88	make sync-check
89	```
90	
91	Full workflow: [Adding vendor skills](https://daviddwlee84.github.io/agent-skills/workflows/adding-vendor-skills/).
92	
93	**Dependencies:** `gh` (GitHub CLI, authenticated) and `yq` (YAML processor).
94	
95	## Docs site
96	
97	The docs site is built with MkDocs Material + `mkdocs-llmstxt` + `mkdocs-copy-to-llm`.
98	
99	```bash
100	uv sync --extra docs
101	make docs-serve         # http://127.0.0.1:8000/
102	make docs-build         # produces ./site/
103	```
104	
105	Deployed automatically to GitHub Pages on push to `main` via [`.github/workflows/docs.yml`](.github/workflows/docs.yml).
106	
107	If you want to apply the same docs stack to your own project, see [Downstream docs stack recipe](https://daviddwlee84.github.io/agent-skills/reference/docs-stack-recipe/).
108	
109	## Adding a new local skill
110	
111	Use the bundled scaffolder (recommended — seeds the agentskills.io best-practice template):
112	
113	```bash
114	bash skills/local/skill-author/scripts/new-skill.sh <skill-name>
115	bash skills/local/skill-author/scripts/lint-skill.sh skills/local/<skill-name>
116	```
117	
118	Or with the upstream init:
119	
120	```bash
121	cd skills/local
122	npx skills@latest init [skill-name]
123	```
124	
125	See [Creating local skills](https://daviddwlee84.github.io/agent-skills/workflows/creating-local-skills/) for the layout rules and authoring guidance.
